CHIEF COMPLAINT

Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. The patient reports that he was doing some yard work in the last week or so and started to feel really tired and short of breath. He believes that he caught his first cold in the last few weeks and that it has gotten worse. The patient reports that he has been doing well with his depression, but would like to start on a medical regiment for it. He has been monitoring his blood pressure at home, but not as much on weekends. His wife got him into barre classes to help him relax.

The patient denies any history of seasonal allergies. He reports that he feels short of breath when lifting or carrying heavy bags, but denies any shortness of breath at rest. He denies fevers, coughing up anything, muscle aches, joint pain, fatigue, nausea or vomiting.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fever.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath.
• Cardiovascular: Reports palpitations.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports joint pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Strongly regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops or rubs.
Respiratory: Scattered ronchi bilaterally on auscultation.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest x-ray obtained today is unremarkable without airspace disease or pneumonia.
Hemoglobin A1c 8.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Andrew Campbell is a 59-year-old male who presents today with an upper respiratory infection. I believe this to be viral syndrome based on his symptoms and examination findings today. We will send a COVID test just to make sure that he does not have COVID-19. I would like to see him again in about 4 months for another hemoglobin A1c.

For his depression, we discussed this today and he would like to continue with psychotherapy in the future if needed.

For his type 2 diabetes, I want to increase his metformin to 1000 mg twice daily and order another hemoglobin A1c in 4 months.

For his hypertension, we discussed this today and we will continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. We will also order a lipid panel today.

Patient wishes to refill lisinopril 20 mg daily today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Andrea Roberts is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history significant for rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux who presents today for her annual exam. She has been walking and exercising as recommended and has been doing yoga. She reports that this has helped with her arthritis. She denies any joint pain or stiffness over the last year.

Regarding her methotrexate, she reports that she is still taking it once weekly and denies any issues with it.

She has been experiencing palpitations again. The last one was about a week ago. She notes that when she starts to get stressed, they start to flare up again. She has been trying meditation and running with her dog to try and relieve the stress but it hasn't really been working.

Regarding her atrial fibrillation, she notes that she is still having palpitations. She notes that when she starts to get stressed, they start to flare up again. She has been trying meditation and running with her dog to try and relieve the stress but it hasn't really been working.

Regarding her reflux, she reports that cutting out soda has helped but she still experiences some reflux symptoms. Her medication seems to be helping too as she hasn't had a flare up in over 5 months.

She endorses nasal congestion due to allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports well.
• Cardiovascular: Endorses palpitations.
• Respiratory: Endorses nasal congestion.

Emergency room follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Albert Powell is a 62-year-old male who presents today for emergency room follow-up. The patient reports that he was not staying on top of his blood sugar readings and felt woozy over the weekend. He was concerned and his wife wanted to take him to the emergency room. The patient reports that his blood sugar was elevated at that time. He denies being admitted to the hospital, but was seen by a physician who recommended dietary modifications.

The patient reports that he has been doing well since returning home from the visit. He notes that he has been following his diet more closely since then. The patient notes that he has been busy during the week, but less consistent on weekends.

Regarding his kidney transplant, the patient reports that he is taking immunotherapy medications as prescribed and has been diligent about it. His last visit with Dr. Reyes was 3 weeks ago and everything seemed to be fine at that time.

Regarding his depression, the patient reports that it has been a tough year-and-a-half, but he has been doing well with it as long as he finds some time to relax in the afternoon.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Respiratory: Denies lightheadedness or dizziness.

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Lawrence Walker is a 62-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for complaints of shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 10 days ago. He reports that he has noticed swelling in his legs. He also reports that he feels lethargic. His shortness of breath is worse when he walks up a flight of stairs. He denies chest pain, fever, chills, cough, abdominal pain, and belly pain.

Mr. Walker reports that he has been doing well with his diabetes and has been monitoring his blood sugars during the week. However, he admits to forgetting to monitor them on weekends due to being busy with house parties and eating salty foods.

Regarding his depression, Mr. Walker reports that it has been a crazy year and a half. He has tried natural solutions such as stretching outdoors every morning in the summer but now that the weather has changed he is looking for alternatives. He is not ready to try any medications at this time.

Regarding his reflux, Mr. Walker reports that he has been making lifestyle modifications by cutting back on red bull and caffeine and reducing alcohol intake during the holiday season.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports lethargy.
• Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath with exertion.
• Respiratory: Reports bilateral crackles at the bases.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 3 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border.
Respiratory: Crackles bilaterally at the bases.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Chest x-ray was reviewed by the nurse prior to this visit and appears normal without evidence of airspace disease.
Laboratory results were reviewed by the nurse prior to this visit and are within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:

Shortness of breath.

His laboratory results were reviewed by the nurse prior to this visit and are within normal limits without evidence for infection or inflammation present.
- Medical Treatment: I have discussed these findings with him today in detail and we have discussed treatment options available for him today including medical treatment options such as Lasix 40 mg daily which will be initiated today as well as lifestyle modifications including weight monitoring daily until weight loss is achieved or weight gain occurs again which will be initiated today as well.

- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with all recommended medical treatment options.

Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

She has been vaccinated and has been able to see her grandchildren again, go to more birthday parties, which she reports has been fantastic. She has been going to therapy once a week for the past year. She notes that virtual therapy was a bit of a struggle, but she feels like in-person therapy really helps her. She does have a good support system at home with her husband and her children are right down the street from her.

Regarding her blood pressure, she notes that they have been doing well since last year. She uses the blood pressure cuff once a day and they seem pretty normal. She is taking lisinopril 20 mg daily as prescribed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports well.
• Cardiovascular: Reports no chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Respiratory: Reports no nasal congestion.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports no abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard in the left lower sternal border.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Electrocardiogram stable in comparison to last year.
note.assessment_and_plan:

1. Depression.
Elizabeth Peterson is doing well with her strategies for managing depression. I do not think we need to start any medication at this time unless she feels differently.

Everything looks fine now. We will continue lisinopril 20 mg daily as prescribed and I want her to continue to watch her blood pressures as well. If they start rising, I want her to contact me.

She is due for a mammogram today.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in his left arm or hand.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports constant left shoulder and left elbow pain.
Neurological: Denies any numbness or tingling.

Impingement syndrome of the left shoulder.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Cradle cap.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Randy Gutierrez is a 9-month-old male who presents today for evaluation of a runny nose, congestion, cough, and ear pain. The onset of his symptoms began last night. He has been experiencing a runny nose and congestion. He also has been pulling on his ears and rubbing at his nose. His mother notes that he has been irritable and is having difficulty sleeping. She notes that he has had a low-grade fever today with a rectal temperature of 100.3 degrees Fahrenheit. His appetite has been variable, but he did eat about 7 ounces from the bottle this morning.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Low-grade fever.
• Respiratory: Runny nose, congestion, cough.
• Ear: Ear pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Ears: No discharge or erythema.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Today Randy Gutierrez was evaluated in the clinic for runny nose, congestion, cough, and ear pain.

His examination was unremarkable except for erythema of the ears.

INSTRUCTIONS

Continue to monitor his symptoms. If they worsen or persist beyond one week, contact us for further evaluation.

Cradle cap is likely due to an overgrowth of yeast in the scalp. I recommended using Head & Shoulders shampoo twice weekly to help prevent cradle cap from recurring in the future. Continue to use a soft brush to remove scales from his scalp as well as baby oil to help soften them.

Medication prescribed today:
- Zarbee's Children's Cough & Cold Formula (1/2 tsp)
- Baby Vick's Ointment (1/2 tsp)
- Agave Nectar (as needed)

Acne.

She reports that she has been using Persa-Gel and washing her face regularly, which is somewhat helpful. She denies any associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. She denies additional past medical history.

She lives with her parents and sister. They have a dog, bird, and bunnies. She is in 7th grade and active in basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing. She wears sunscreen in the summer SPF 30.

She denies any significant family medical history.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: No additional past medical history.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Lives with parents and sister. They have a dog, bird, and bunnies. She is in 7th grade and active in basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing.

FAMILY HISTORY

No significant family medical history.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Skin: Multiple benign nevi on the trunk and extremities. Scattered skin colored papules. Open and closed comedones. Erythmateous papules on the face primarily on the forehead with also some on the central cheeks and chin. The chest and back are relatively spared.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kayla Ward is a 15-year-old female who presents for a new visit today due to acne on the face that has been present for approximately 2 years.
- Medical Reasoning: Mild to moderate acne mostly comodonal with small inflammatory component.
- Medical Treatment Plan: Start with topical therapy first every morning wash her face with a mild cleanser then use a moisturizer labeled "noncomedogenic" with sunscreen SPF 30 or higher this means it won't clog your pores now in the evening wash your face with the same cleanser allow it to dry apply adapalene 0.1% cream in a thin layer to the areas you generally get acne i want you to start off using this a few nights a week slowly work up to using it every night if it is very expensive or not covered by insurance you can try different gel over the counter you can follow that with clean and clear persa-gel in a thin layer or where you generally get acne then noncomedogenic moisturizer it may also cause some dryness or irritation we will see if she has any progress over the next six months follow up at that time.

Breast reduction.

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia, presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments, but the minimal relief. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing back pain since high school. She has been going to the chiropractor for a few years and notes that she does have bra strap indentations in her shoulders. She also notes that she experiences numbness and tingling in her hands and nipple pain. She also reports that she is currently studying psychology.

The patient denies any history of breast cancer in her family. She has not had any mammograms yet, but her mother was diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40 and recommended she start mammograms at age 30.

She denies tobacco use, alcohol use, or illicit drug use. She does take propranolol for migraine prevention.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports weight loss over the past few months.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports back pain, neck pain, and shoulder pain.
• Neurological: Reports numbness and tingling in the hands.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Breast: Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia, presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments, but the minimal relief. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Status post mitral valve repair.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ms. Sanchez is a 58-year-old female who presents today for status post mitral valve repair done on 8/3/2020. She reports that she was having a rough time before surgery, but she feels much better now. She reports that she is still experiencing chest pain, but her breathing gets shallow. She notes that when she feels this way, she slows down and takes it easy for a few minutes until the symptoms resolve. She notes that the episodes last only a few minutes and then resolve for a while. She notes that this happens often enough for her to notice.

She denies any new symptoms today.

She reports taking her medications regularly, but notes that there are many extra pills now and that she has been trying to keep up with them with the help of a reminder app.

She reports taking Coumadin 4 mg daily, Lasix 40 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily.

She denies any side effects from her medications at all.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
Respiratory: Reports shallow breathing.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Head and Neck: No jugular venous distention detected.
Respiratory: Reduced breath sounds bilaterally. Auscultation and percussion are clear bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular rhythm.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

ECG taken on 12/26/2020 reveals atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response. T-wave inversion anteriorly. Compared to the previous study, there are no significant changes.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Status post mitral valve repair.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient is doing well from a cardiac standpoint at this time. Her ECG taken today reveals atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response compared to the previous study which showed t-wave inversion anteriorly. There were no significant changes noted between studies.
- Patient Education: I advised the patient that many people with atrial fibrillation are able to keep it under control with medicine and lifestyle changes.
- Medical Treatment: Continue current medications as prescribed including Coumadin 4 mg daily, Lasix 40 mg daily, and Atenolol 50 mg daily every day as tolerated by the patient.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Judy Gomez is a 61-year-old female who presents today for ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis. She reports that she has been doing well since the last visit, but she did take an extra prednisone tablet once a week due to increased pain in her feet. She notes that she has a desk job and moving around more often can cause her pain to increase. She discontinued methotrexate due to concerns about vaccine efficacy, but resumed it after calling into the hotline and was told to continue taking it. She notes that she has been experiencing bruising on her skin, which she attributes to the prednisone.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports joint pain.
Cardiovascular: Reports bruising.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Constitutional: Well-nourished female.
Neurological: Normal motor strength in all extremities. Normal sensation in all extremities.
Musculoskeletal: Mild bilateral hand swelling. No erythema or warmth. No joint effusion or deformity. No muscle atrophy. Normal range of motion in all joints bilaterally.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient is a 61-year-old female who presents today for ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

Medical Reasoning:
- The patient is doing well since the last visit, but she did take an extra prednisone tablet once a week due to increased pain in her feet.
- She discontinued methotrexate due to concerns about vaccine efficacy, but resumed it after calling into the hotline and was told to continue taking it.
- She has been experiencing bruising on her skin, which she attributes to the prednisone.
- Her constitutional exam was unremarkable.
- Her neurological exam was unremarkable.
- Her musculoskeletal exam revealed mild bilateral hand swelling without erythema or warmth, no joint effusion or deformity, no muscle atrophy, and normal range of motion in all joints bilaterally.
- We are moving along with her treatment nicely with decreasing prednisone dose and continuing methotrexate as needed for pain control. We will discontinue prednisone today and schedule blood work for next visit.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

New worrisome heart murmur.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Diana Scott is a 100-year-old female who presents today for a new patient evaluation. She reports that her doctor has noted a new worrisome heart murmur. She denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. She does report severe leg pain, which she has been taking pain medication for. She also reports lightheadedness and dizziness, which she treats with meclizine. She denies fevers, chills, irregular heartbeats, or passing out.

She notes that her symptoms have improved from 70-80% since last month. Her symptoms were completely absent prior to last month.

She reports that she has had multiple surgeries in the past including hip replacement and knee replacement.

FAMILY HISTORY

The patient reports that her son had a myocardial infarction. Her brother had a stroke and is diabetic. Her older sister has an unknown heart problem.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she does not smoke.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Endorses dyspnea on exertion.
Neurological: Endorses lightheadedness and dizziness.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Constitutional Elderly Otherwise No Acute Distress.
Cardiovascular: S1 and S2 are preserved with a normal rate and regular rhythm. There is a 4/6 systolic murmur at the right upper sternal border with mild radiation to the carotids.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
The patient's EKG today shows sinus rhythm with frequent PVCs as well as an anterior septum infarct pattern.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diana Scott is a 100-year-old female who presents today for a new patient evaluation.
Probable one cardiac murmur.
Diana has a 4/6 systolic murmur at the upper right sternal border with mild radiation to the carotids. This is most likely representative of aortic stenosis, for symptoms could be due to severe aortic stenosis. However, her S2 is relatively preserved, which would be more consistent with moderate diastolic dysfunction. Some of her outside records do note diastolic dysfunction, so it is possible she did have an echocardiogram at some point in the past. She does not appear significantly volume overloaded today.
Next problem: PVCs.
The referral mentioned tachycardia. Her EKG today shows sinus rhythm with frequent PVCs as well as an anterior septum infarct pattern. She does not have any significant palpitations and we will check an echocardiogram to assess overall cardiac structure and function depending on results as well as the severity of her aortic stenosis, we will need to consider an ischemic evaluation or further possibly a heart monitor to assess overall burden of the PVCs. At this point she's asymptomatic so we will start with the echocardiogram only.
Hypolipidemia is managed by her PCP.
Due to bilateral leg pain over the last month considered TAVR evaluation following echocardiogram.
Statin could be indicated due to bilateral leg pain over the last month.
Lightheadedness/dizziness treated with meclizine for this reason it is possible that some of her lightheadedness and dizziness are related to the Aortic Stenosis we will do an echocardiogram as noted above. PVCS on her EKG could be contributing but she does not feel palpitations we will consider a monitor but start with the echocardiogram first as noted above.
Follow up in 3-4 weeks after echocardiogram done to discuss results and next steps.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Gregory Hernandez is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that he has had this non-healing ulcer for approximately 2 months. He states that it has recently become red and is draining. The patient was concerned about how it has healed. He denies any trauma to his foot, but believes he may have gotten it from walking barefoot on the beach. The patient reports that he did see his primary care provider before coming in today and they started him on antibiotics, but he did not pick them up from the pharmacy yet. He does not recall the name of the medication prescribed for him.

The patient reports that he has been taking his diabetes medication, but does not check his sugars all the time. He is not sure what his last A1C was, but believes it was around 10.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fever.
• Skin: Reports redness and drainage of right foot ulcer.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Skin: Examination of the right foot reveals a 1 by 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. There is some redness and drainage present. There is edema around it.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot reveals no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Gregory Hernandez is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer.

Diagnosis:
• Non-healing diabetic foot ulcer.
• Possible osteomyelitis.
• Diabetes mellitus type II.
• Hyperglycemia.
• Edema.
• Infection.
• Osteomyelitis.
• Hypertension.
• Hyperlipidemia.
• Obesity.

Plan:
The patient will be referred for an ABI ankle brachial index to determine blood supply in his feet to see if we can actually heal this ulcer. We will also perform debridement today to remove some dead tissue and prescribe clindamycin 400 mg twice daily for 7 days to try to get rid of this infection which he currently does have and that will get rid of some of that redness and drainage that's happening now. We discussed with him wearing a surgical shoe while this is happening as well as seeing him back in 2 weeks for another debridement at that time we'll just take a look at how the tissue is doing at that point.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Stephanie Morales is a 36-year-old female today complaining of left ankle pain. She reports that she was walking to her car and slipped on some snow and ice. She fell and her left ankle turned underneath her. She was able to get up afterwards but it was very sore and started swelling. She has been experiencing pain with weight-bearing.

The patient reports that she has been taking ibuprofen, ice, and elevation for pain and swelling. She denies any bleeding or bruising.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left ankle pain.
Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the left leg.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No bruits.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from before.
Gastrointestinal: Normal bowel sounds, no tenderness to palpation of the abdomen.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the left ankle reveals tenderness over the lateral malleolus as well as tenderness over the fifth metatarsal. There is some swelling, redness, and pain with valgus stressing of the ankle.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient presents today for evaluation of left ankle pain. I have diagnosed her with an ankle sprain today. I would like to order an x-ray of her left ankle due to some tenderness over this bone which may be a sign of a fracture. We will start her in an air splint until we receive the x-rays back today. We will avoid weight-bearing until then to ensure there is no fracture present. I have prescribed naprosyn 500 mg twice daily for pain control until then as well as elevation and ice application for pain control at home.

Regarding her diabetes, we discussed this last year when we last saw each other. Her hemoglobin A1c was 6.8 last time I looked at Epic which is really good! She has been doing a great job with diet modifications as well as regular blood sugar monitoring through home testing. We discussed cutting out sweets and sugars as well as increasing physical activity which she has been doing regularly since then so it sounds like she's doing a great job with that! Her next eye exam for diabetes checkup is due in the next couple weeks so we will schedule that appointment today if she hasn't already done so.
Regarding her hypertension, we discussed this last year when we last saw each other also. Her blood pressure today looks pretty good at 120/70 mmHg but she does need a refill on Norvasc today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right foot wound.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Wayne Jenkins is a 43-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for a sore on his right foot that is not healing. The patient purchased a new pair of shoes to travel with and the neuropathy he has been experiencing did not feel that they were too tight at first. However, a blister formed on his right foot which soon became a wound. He was seen by his PCP who placed him on antibiotics which he completed yesterday. The patient denies any changes to the appearance of the wound, pain or drainage. Occasionally, he has issues with stability, which was a primary purpose of purchasing these shoes. He denies fever or chills.

The patient reports neuropathy.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking antibiotics (completed yesterday).

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
Musculoskeletal: Reports issues with stability.
Neurological: Reports neuropathy.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: Palpable bilateral femoral and popliteal pulses. No palpable DP or PT pulses but Doppler signs are present.
MSK: Examination of the right foot reveals a 1x2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the right 5th metatarsophalangeal joint. There is some yellow slough present with minimal granulation tissue. There is no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there is no evidence of fluid collection. There is no necrosis present and there is no odor.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was reviewed in clinic today and shows no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right diabetic foot ulcer.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for evaluation of a diabetic foot ulcer on his right foot that has not healed despite antibiotic therapy and debridement in clinic yesterday.
- Medical Treatment: I have reviewed the results today and we will continue this until we see the wound shrinking and nice pink tissue present. We will continue this once daily with collagenase ointment applied to the wound covered with dry sterile dressing until we see improvement in healing. We will also continue wearing surgical shoe to take pressure off area until we see improvement in healing.
- Patient Education: I have discussed treatment options with him today as well as importance of keeping diabetes under control in order to heal this ulcer.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Hill is a pleasant 44-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of back pain. The onset of his back pain began approximately 30 years ago when he fell off a roof and sustained what he believes was a fracture. He has been unable to play football due to pain. He denies any history of trauma to his back. The patient reports that his symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past month, and he has been unable to tolerate sitting or standing for prolonged periods of time. He notes that his symptoms are worse with coughing, sneezing, and bending forward. The patient reports that he has tried NSAIDs in the past without relief.

The patient denies any numbness or tingling in his lower extremities or any weakness in his legs.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports lower back pain radiating down left leg.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in lower extremities or weakness in legs.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the spine reveals tenderness over L4 vertebrae with positive pain on palpation. There is no bony abnormalities, erythema, or ecchymosis present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

MRI of the lumbar spine reveals a disk herniation at L4-5 vertebrae with nerve root impingement.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Matthew Hill is a pleasant 44-year-old male who presents today for the evaluation of back pain.

The patient endorses low back pain radiating down left leg. This is associated with left hip pain, left leg pain into the calf and big toe. His symptoms have been progressively worsening over the past month and he has been unable to tolerate sitting or standing for prolonged periods of time. He notes that his symptoms are worse with coughing, sneezing, and bending forward.
MRI of the lumbar spine reveals a disk herniation at L4-5 vertebrae with nerve root impingement.

After reviewing this information today, I have had a lengthy discussion with him regarding his current symptoms and treatment options available to him today. We discussed epidural steroid injection as an option today as well as continued physical therapy referral.
I have recommended an epidural steroid injection today for him as well as continued physical therapy referral.
We discussed this treatment plan further and he agrees.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Recent blood work.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Walker is a 68-year-old female who presents today for recent blood work. She reports that her primary care provider recently ordered blood work and informed her that she has hepatitis C. She is surprised because she has been feeling fine. She denies any history of intravenous drug use, but admits to heavy alcohol use in the past. She currently drinks approximately 1 beer per day, more on the weekends. She also admits to smoking 1-2 cigarettes per day, previously 1 to 1.5 packs per day.

The patient reports that she has been feeling very tired at the end of the day after working, but otherwise feels good.

PAST HISTORY

Personal history: Intravenous drug use over 15 years ago; currently smoking 1-2 cigarettes per day, previously 1 to 1.5 packs per day; history of heavy alcohol use, but now drinks approximately 1 beer per day, more on the weekends.
Family history: Hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is a workaholic and tends to be busy with work.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Reports fatigue at the end of the day after working.
Gastrointestinal: Reports constipation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

General Appearance: Appears in no distress.
Skin: No jaundice.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with a 2/6 systolic murmur appreciated.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
HCV antibody was positive. Liver panel shows elevated AST at 39 but ALT, albumin and total bilirubin were all within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Jacqueline Walker is a 68-year-old female who presents today for recent blood work. Her HCV antibody test was positive and her liver panel showed an elevated AST at 39 but her ALT, albumin and total bilirubin were all within normal limits. Her initial labs are consistent with hepatitis C so based on what I just discussed with her today we will confirm the diagnosis with additional bloodwork including checking HCV RNA and also HCV genotype. We will also determine the severity of her liver disease by ordering a special ultrasound to check for fibrosis of the liver. With this information we will be able to know how to proceed as far as treatment.
I have reviewed this information with her today and answered any questions she may have had.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Headaches.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julie Jenkins is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of headaches. She has been experiencing headaches since she was a teenager and they used to be around her when she would have her menstrual periods. However, as she got older, she noticed that they were not limited to her menstrual periods anymore and they are now more frequent and severe. She has also noticed that they seem to get worse when she is exercising. She denies any numbness or tingling to her hands or feet or face.

The patient reports that her headaches are located on the right side and it even seems like it's behind her eye. They present as a pulsing sensation. She also reports that she has been experiencing ringing in her ears for a few months now and then what really scared her is that now she's starting to get some blurred vision on the side of her vision.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient enjoys running and wears New Balance or Asics shoes.

MEDICATIONS

She denies taking any medications at this time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Neurological: Headaches, ringing in ears, blurred vision.
• Ophthalmologic: Blurred vision.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neurological: Cranial nerves 1-12 are intact including normal cranial reflexes. Gait is normal.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Neurological Exam: Cranial nerves 1-12 are intact including normal cranial reflexes.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Idiopathic intracranial hypertension.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient’s symptoms are concerning for idiopathic intracranial hypertension. This is a condition where there is increased pressure in the head in the brain without any known cause for it. This can lead to permanent changes in vision if left untreated.
• Medical Treatment: We discussed treatment options today with the patient today. We discussed that we will need an MRI of the brain to confirm this diagnosis and we will also need a spinal tap to help decrease pressure in the brain. We will also refer her to a neuro-ophthalmologist for a complete eye exam today as well.
• Patient Education: I explained all of these options today and answered any questions she had regarding them.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with all recommended medical treatment.

Neck pain.

Jack Torres is a 40-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of neck pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago after he was in a motor vehicle accident where he hit the back of his head and neck. He reports that his neck went forward and his head went forward quickly. He has been experiencing neck pain ever since. The patient rates his pain as an 8 out of 10 on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain possible. The patient states that the pain is not constant, but it worsens with movement of his neck. He denies any headaches, but does report some early morning headaches. The patient denies any upper back or shoulder pain, as well as hearing or visual disturbances.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that he played football years ago without any neck issues.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that he has been taking ibuprofen for his neck pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fever.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports neck pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neurological: Normal strength in all extremities. Positive pain to palpation of the soft tissues of the neck. Positive pain with flexion and extension of the cervical spine. Positive pain with lateral bending.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray of cervical spine obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Neck strain.
Treatments we are going to treat this conservatively today. I am going to put him on anti-inflammatory motrin six hundred milligrams and he's going to take that every six to eight hours as needed. I also want him to take flexeril ten milligrams every twelve hours as needed.
I also want him to try and relax his neck today and be conservative with how he moves about and everything like that.
I also want us to order an MRI just because he did not go to the hospital or anything like that I just want to make sure that there isn't any impingement on any nerves or anything like that.
I think we should refer him either physical therapy or chiropractic once we get the results from the MRI just to make sure there isn't any impingement on any nerves or anything like that.
Patient understands.

Right shoulder pain.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

For the patient's current complaints, I have reviewed his examination findings today and have discussed them with him. His symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy. note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

William Smith is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right elbow pain. The onset of his symptoms began 3 weeks ago after he started playing tennis more frequently. He denies any trauma to the right elbow. The patient reports that the pain is localized to the lateral aspect of his right elbow and is described as sharp, shooting, and throbbing. The patient states that the pain is worse with movement and better with rest. He has tried taking Tylenol and ibuprofen but these do not help with his symptoms. He has also tried icing his right elbow but this does not help either.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in the right arm or hand.
Cardiovascular: Reports grade 3 systolic ejection murmur.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Grade 3 systolic ejection murmur to the left sternal border unchanged from prior exam.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right elbow reveals moderate lateral epicondylar tenderness. Pain with passive range of motion of the right elbow, no palpable joint effusion, mild pain with resisted extension of the right wrist.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow today shows no acute fracture or other bony abnormality. There is no malalignment or sign of joint effusion.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Acute lateral epicondylitis of the right elbow.
- Medical Reasoning: This is likely due to overuse likely from increased tennis activity which normally would be good but maybe we are overdoing it a little bit.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I explained to him that resting his arm as much as possible would be beneficial for him at this time. I advised him to stop playing tennis for 4-6 weeks and avoid repetitive stress in that arm as well.
- Medical Treatment: I recommended that he ice his right elbow for 20 minutes at least 3 times per day which should reduce his pain and inflammation. I also prescribed Ultram 50 mg once per day for pain management.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with my recommendations.

2. Diabetes type two.
- Medical Reasoning: His blood sugars are a bit off due to eating too many Cadbury eggs during Easter weekend last week.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed how we need to make some adjustments in order to get his blood sugars back into control.
- Medical Treatment: We increased his metformin dosage from 500 mg twice daily to 1000 mg twice daily today. We will check his blood sugar twice daily for the next two weeks and then we will reevaluate him at that time if needed.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with my recommendations.

3. Mild intermittent asthma.
- Medical Reasoning: His asthma remains under good control at this time so we will continue on Flovent twice daily as well as albuterol as needed today without any changes needed at this time.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed how he can use albuterol as tolerated today without any changes needed at this time, however, he does need a refill on albuterol so I have written him a prescription for a refill today which he can pick up at his pharmacy today if needed.
- Medical Treatment: Prescribed albuterol refill today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Asthma.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Lewis is a 66-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for worsening asthma symptoms. The patient reports that she has been experiencing shortness of breath, coughing, and wheezing for the past 6 months. She notes that her symptoms tend to worsen when she gets sick with a cold and that she has had several exacerbations in the past year. She also notes that she has had several visits to urgent care and her primary care provider due to her asthma symptoms. She reports that she has been prescribed prednisone in the past, but does not remember the exact dose or duration of treatment. She also mentions that she has had an exacerbation approximately 1 month ago.

The patient denies any history of seasonal allergies or smoking tobacco products. She does report that she occasionally goes to bars where smoking is allowed inside, which bothers her.

The patient enjoys hiking and notes that she has been unable to do so due to her asthma symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Respiratory: Shortness of breath, coughing, wheezing.
• Constitutional: Fatigue.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs or gallops.
Respiratory: Diminished lung sounds throughout with occasional expiratory wheeze bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pulmonary function test obtained today is consistent with asthma.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Asthma.
• Medical Reasoning: Betty Lewis is a 66-year-old female who presents today for worsening asthma symptoms. Her symptoms have been consistent with moderate intermittent asthma based on her history and pulmonary function test results today. We discussed this with the patient today and reviewed treatment options including inhaled steroid inhaler use as well as albuterol inhaler use as needed.
• Medical Treatment: We discussed treatment options today including inhaled steroid inhaler use as well as albuterol inhaler use as needed. We reviewed the importance of using the inhaled steroid inhaler consistently in order to prevent daily symptoms from needing rescue inhaler use less frequently. We also discussed how we can work on avoiding triggers such as cats at her aunt's house which may be causing exacerbations of her asthma symptoms.
• Patient Education: I explained to Betty Lewis how important it is for her to be consistent with her inhaled steroid inhaler use in order to prevent daily symptoms from needing rescue inhaler use less frequently. I also explained how we can work on avoiding triggers such as cats at her aunt's house which may be causing exacerbations of her asthma symptoms.
• Patient Agreements: Betty Lewis understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kenneth King is a 44-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 5 days ago when he was out on his boat skiing and did a jump and twisted when he landed. He denies hearing anything pop or feeling anything pop at the time. He was able to get out of the water by himself but it was very sore to climb up and any kind of squatting or bending is really pretty sore. He has had no previous history of knee injuries.

The patient reports that he has been taking lisinopril 20 mg once a day for his hypertension. His blood pressure at home has been about 125/80 most of the days. He denies any side effects from lisinopril.

The patient reports that he has been taking Aleve twice a day for pain relief, as well as applying a cold pack to his right knee.

He denies any numbness or tingling in his foot.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in his foot.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No lymphadenopathy appreciated.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs appreciated.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals ecchymosis, edema, effusion present. There is pain to palpation of the right medial knee. There is decreased range of motion bilaterally with negative varus and valgus tests, negative Lachman sign, palpable dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Lisinopril 20 mg once a day.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee pain:
- Right medial collateral ligament strain.
- Order an x-ray of the right knee today to rule out any fractures which I do not think we will need to proceed with surgery at this time.
- Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain and swelling management today.
- Refer patient to physical therapy for strengthening exercises today.
- Continue lisinopril 20 mg once daily as prescribed today.
- Order lipid panel today for health maintenance purposes today.
- Tetanus shot due for health maintenance purposes today.
Hypertension:
Continue lisinopril 20 mg once daily as prescribed today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Kyle Rodriguez is a 57-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of an incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule. The patient reports that he first noticed his cough when he was loading horses and that it has been ongoing for approximately 3 months. He notes that he typically does not get sick and denies any recent flares of his rheumatoid arthritis. The patient reports that he exercises regularly, biking approximately 2-3 times per week. He stopped smoking tobacco 7 years ago.

The patient denies any shortness of breath or chest pain.

FAMILY HISTORY

The patient reports that his mother has a history of breast cancer, but is doing well.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports taking methotrexate 7.5 mg every week.

ALLERGIES

No allergies specified.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Blood Pressure: 124/76 mmHg.; Heart Rate: 70 beats per minute.; Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths per minute.; Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air.; Body Temperature: Afebrile.
EXTREMITIES: Skin is pink, warm, and dry. No edema to lower extremities. Swelling to third digit on each hand which can be normal for somebody who has RA however pulses are intact in all extremities and capillary refill is brisk.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
CT scan of chest demonstrates a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule.
• Medical Reasoning: The CT scan of the chest demonstrates a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe. The appearance is smooth with no evidence of emphysematous disease present which is good. Given his smoking history, I believe it would be best to remove this nodule via video-assisted thoracoscopy.
• Medical Treatment Plan: We will order pulmonary function tests to check and establish a baseline for your lung function today. We will also schedule a PET-CT to determine if this nodule is metabolically active meaning if it lights up it can suggest that it’s cancer or inflammatory. We will proceed with removal during or via video-assisted thoracoscopy which means it’s just going to be three small incisions made on the side of your right chest. You will be under general anesthesia and it’ll take about an hour and a half or so post procedure you’ll be admitted and you will have a chest tube in until the following day and we’ll take that out then at bedside most likely you’ll be in the hospital for one night and go home the next day.
• Patient Education/ Counseling: I explained all treatment options available to him today including medical treatment options as well as surgical options, risks, benefits, alternatives, etc., as well as what to expect post-procedure including pain management, recovery time, etc., today as well as what to expect after discharge from surgery today.
• Patient Agreements/Consents: Patient understands all medical treatment options available today including medical treatment options as well as surgical options, risks, benefits, alternatives, etc., as well as what to expect post-procedure including pain management, recovery time, etc., today as well as what to expect after discharge from surgery today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Difficulty swallowing.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Tyler Green is a 56-year-old male who presents today complaining of difficulty swallowing. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 4-5 weeks ago. He states that he has noticed something is always stuck in his throat and that it is bothersome at times. He notes that he has to wash down solid foods on occasion, but does not have to worry about choking. He denies coughing with his symptoms, but does report that it is more with solids than liquids. He denies any blood in his stools or vomiting.

Mr. Green reports that he has been compliant with his diabetes and continues to take metformin 500 mg twice a day. He reports that he checks his blood sugars once in a while, but estimates that he checks them about 80% of the time. His most recent hemoglobin A1c was 7.4 and they discussed improving his diet and exercise at their last visit.

Regarding his hypertension, Mr. Green reports that he takes Norvasc as prescribed and checks his blood pressure at home approximately once a week or more frequently if time allows. His most recent blood pressure was 120/50 in the office today.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
Respiratory: Denies hemoptysis.
Gastrointestinal: Denies hematochezia or vomiting.
Musculoskeletal: Denies back pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No lymphadenopathy, no masses, no erythema, no bruits.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: No murmurs heard on auscultation of the heart.
Abdomen: Epigastric tenderness to palpation.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Tyler Green is a 56-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of difficulty swallowing.

Medical Reasoning:
The patient's symptoms are concerning for esophageal stricture due to the nature of the symptoms and lack of coughing with dysphagia. Esophageal stricture can be caused by scar tissue from prior esophageal surgery or radiation therapy, inflammation from GERD, or other causes such as eosinophilic esophagitis or achalasia. The patient's history of diabetes may also be contributing to this symptomatology as well as weight loss which may be related to diabetic neuropathy affecting the esophagus leading to dysphagia.

Patient Agreements:
The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan today.

Right ankle pain and instability.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Cook is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right ankle pain and instability. The patient reports that his son Sean, who is 10 years old, was playing basketball at the courts and was more aggressive than the other players. The patient went up for a shot and Sean found him while he was going for a lap. When the patient came down, he landed awkwardly and rolled and twisted his right ankle. He notes that he has been experiencing bruising and swelling in his right ankle. The patient reports that he recently got back into working out and had been in a good rhythm going to the gym, but now he is having trouble walking due to instability in his right ankle.

The patient also reports that he plans to coach his son’s basketball team in April 2022. He enjoys working out and recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Skin: Reports right ankle bruising and swelling.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right ankle reveals exquisite tenderness laterally. There is some tenderness over the medial deltoid region. There is swelling on the lateral side of the ankle. No epidermolysis of skin is intact. Brisk capillary refill.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays were obtained today, not yet reviewed.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lateral malleolar fracture of the right ankle.
Medical Reasoning: This appears to be a displaced lateral malleolus at Weber C level on x-ray without evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.
Medical Treatment: I have discussed this diagnosis with the patient today, who understands that this will require surgery to stabilize it. We discussed options for treatment including plate fixation with screws, which will result in approximately 3 months of non-weight bearing status post-op. We discussed that he may need to sit out for coaching until then but we can get him back on court once healed up again.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with this plan.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jerry Cook is a 45-year-old male who presents today with right ankle pain and instability. The patient reports that his son Sean, who is 10 years old, was playing basketball at the courts and was more aggressive than the other players. The patient went up for a shot and Sean found him while he was going for a lap. When the patient came down, he landed awkwardly and rolled and twisted his right ankle. He notes that he has been experiencing bruising and swelling in his right ankle. The patient reports that he recently got back into working out and had been in a good rhythm going to the gym, but now he is having trouble walking due to instability in his right ankle.

The patient also reports that he plans to coach his son’s basketball team in April 2022. He enjoys working out and recently resumed engaging in a consistent gym routine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain and instability.
Skin: Reports right ankle bruising and swelling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right ankle reveals exquisite tenderness laterally. There is some tenderness over the medial deltoid region. There is swelling on the lateral side of the ankle. No epidermolysis of skin is intact. Brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS

X-rays were obtained today, not yet reviewed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Lateral malleolar fracture of the right ankle.
Medical Reasoning: This appears to be a displaced lateral malleolus at Weber C level on x-ray without evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures.
Medical Treatment: I have discussed this diagnosis with the patient today, who understands that this will require surgery to stabilize it. We discussed options for treatment including plate fixation with screws, which will result in approximately 3 months of non-weight bearing status post-op. We discussed that he may need to sit out for coaching until then but we can get him back on court once healed up again.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with this plan.

Evaluation of facial pain.

The patient denies a history of multiple sclerosis or brain tumors. He does occasionally get headaches, but they are not migraines.

Pain intensity: 10/10.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Neurological: Denies vision changes or weakness in right eye.
• Headache: Reports headaches.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neurological: Sensory examination of the face reveals decreased sensation on the right side compared to the left.

RESULTS
MRI of the head reveals small blood vessel abutting and perhaps even pinching the trigeminal nerve.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient presents today for evaluation of facial pain. MRI of the head reveals small blood vessel abutting and perhaps even pinching the trigeminal nerve which may be causing trigeminal neuralgia.

I have discussed this with him today and we have discussed treatment options including medications such as tegretol which are gabapentin analogs that help reduce excitability of the nerve. We have also discussed surgical options such as decompression surgery to decompress the nerve root cause of compression is due to blood vessel against nerve.
We will start with tegretol first and if this does not work we can discuss surgical options later.
I have prescribed tegretol to start with and we will follow up in one month.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle King is a 44-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began after she caught her ski when she was coming off the lift and fell. She was unable to bear weight immediately after the injury. She reports that her knee feels unstable and that it does not hold her weight. She denies any numbness or tingling in her toes, but she does report that she has some pain with straightening her knee. She denies any leg edema in the ankle.

The patient reports that she is very active with skiing and taking care of her 4-year-old twins. Her husband works a job where he is gone quite a bit.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she is very active with skiing and taking care of her 4-year-old twins. Her husband works a job where he is gone quite a bit.

MEDICATIONS

The patient reports that she takes ibuprofen for pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals edema and effusion over the right knee. There is pain to palpation of the right lateral knee, decreased flexion and extension, positive Lachman sign, palpable dorsalis pedis, and posterior tibial pulse, no leg edema in the ankle.
note.objective_results: RESULTS
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michelle King is a 44-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of her symptoms began after she caught her ski when she was coming off the lift and fell. She was unable to bear weight immediately after the injury. She reports that her knee feels unstable and that it does not hold her weight. She denies any numbness or tingling in her toes, but she does report that she has some pain with straightening her knee. She denies any leg edema in the ankle.
I appreciate some edema and an effusion over the right knee today which hurts when I press on it. There is pain to palpation of the right lateral knee today which also feels unstable as if it will buckle. There is decreased flexion and extension today as well as a positive Lachman sign today which also hurts when I try to straighten all the way at this point in time there is no leg edema in the ankle today.
I have reviewed Michelle's x-ray today which did not show any bony abnormality but I am concerned that Michelle may have ruptured her ACL or anterior cruciate ligament which helps connect and helps your knee move back and forth so I would like to order an MRI just so we can get a good look at what's going on with Michelle's right knee today.
Some people can have a normal physical exam but their ACL can still be torn so I would like to make sure there are no other structures damaged by this accident as well.
The patient reports taking ibuprofen for pain management which has been somewhat helpful but we will continue ibuprofen every 8 hours as needed until we discuss further options at our next visit.
I have recommended Michelle wear a brace for support while we wait for our MRI results.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Neck pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brandon Green is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of neck pain. The patient was involved in 4 motor vehicle accidents. He was fine after the first two accidents. The third motor vehicle accident is when his neck and back pain began. He was in therapy following the second accident. He had surgery after his third accident. He was seen at a pain clinic secondary to neck and back pain.

The patient reports that he has been experiencing neck pain since February of this year, which is when he was coming home from the pain clinic because his neck hurts and his back hurts. The patient denies any numbness, dizziness, or visual disturbances. However, he does report that he has been experiencing fatigue since the accident.

Pain is rated at 12/10 with sharp incapacitating pain that prevents him from working.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fatigue.
• Musculoskeletal: Neck pain, left arm numbness, right leg numbness, left arm spasms.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Neurological: Examination of the extremities reveals decreased strength in the left upper extremity and right lower extremity.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of the neck were obtained today and reviewed by me today. There are no fractures noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Brandon Green is a 46-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of neck pain.

I have reviewed his x-rays today and there are no fractures noted. I have discussed this with him today and we have discussed conservative treatment options as well as additional testing options.
I have recommended that we obtain an MRI of his cervical spine to evaluate for any soft tissue injuries.
We will start him on Robaxin 1500 mg every 6-8 hours to help with muscle relaxation and reduce tension in the area.
We will also refer him to physical therapy for additional treatment options.
If these symptoms do not improve we can consider local injections or referral to pain medicine.

Follow-up of chronic problems.

Carolyn Garcia is a 49-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of her chronic problems. She reports that her osteoarthritis has been flaring up a little bit lately, primarily in her right elbow. She has been sitting at the computer, at the desk more in the office and she does not know if it is being stagnant in that position all day which has increased flare-ups for that. She also reports that she has been typing all day versus writing, so it flares up in both elbows. She denies any other joint pain. She does report numbness and tingling in her hands when she is typing for long periods of time, but she tries to shake out her arms to relieve that sensation.

Regarding gout, she reports that the last episode was about 3 months ago and she had some inflammation of her toe. She states that she has not seen a flare-up since.

She also reports that her psoriasis is under control.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right elbow pain with extension and flexion.
Neurological: Reports numbness and tingling in hands when typing for long periods of time.
note.objective_exam:

Neurological: Examination of the extremities reveals no lower extremity edema. Examination of the scalp reveals erythema and scaling over the left side of the scalp without any tenderness or pain to palpation.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right elbow reveals edema and inflammation of the right olecranon with tenderness and effusion. Pain to palpation of the olecranon bursa with pain with pronation and supination. Pain with flexion and extension.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Autoimmune panel was reviewed today by Dr. [doctor]. There were no signs of systemic arthritis or systemic inflammatory process going on today.
Uric acid level was reviewed today by Dr. [doctor]. The level was elevated.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Carolyn Garcia is a 49-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of her chronic problems.
- Gout: Stable.
- Osteoarthritis: Right elbow pain with extension and flexion.
- Psoriasis: Stable.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's elevated uric acid level warrants further investigation into possible gout flare-ups as well as continued treatment for osteoarthritis due to recent flare-ups.
Medical Treatment Plan:
- Continue colchicine 0.6 mg twice a day as needed for gout flare-ups.
- Order a right elbow x-ray today to evaluate for possible osteoarthritis.
- Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once a day for pain and swelling associated with osteoarthritis today.
- Continue clobetasol cream once daily for scalp psoriasis.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Positive for fever.
• Musculoskeletal: Positive for joint pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Positive for nausea.
• Skin: Positive for rash.
note.objective_exam:

note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Lyme titer is elevated.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michelle Lee is a 31-year-old female with a past medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension who presents today for evaluation of abnormal lab findings. Her labs were reviewed today, and her WBC count was within normal limits. Her Lyme titer was elevated, so we will order further testing today. Her blood sugar levels have been stable with the exception of some highs and lows, but they are within range. She continues to take metformin as prescribed. Her blood pressure has been stable at home with the exception of some high readings, but these have been well-managed by avoiding salty foods.

For her newly diagnosed Lyme disease, I have prescribed doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 3 weeks due to the elevated Lyme titer results today. We will follow up with an infectious disease specialist to discuss further treatment options if needed.

For her type 2 diabetes, I have ordered a hemoglobin A1c today as we need to ensure that there are no changes needed to her current metformin regimen.

For her hypertension, everything appears stable today; however, I would like to order a lipid panel today as well as continue lisinopril 10 mg daily due to continued stability in blood pressure at home.

Patient Agreements:
The patient understands the nature of her medical condition and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluation of high blood sugar.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Hannah Phillips is a 52-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of a high blood sugar. She reports that she has been eating a lot of sweets recently due to the holidays, and this has resulted in her feeling light-headed and seeing spots. She went to the emergency room where she was treated with IV fluids and told to cut out extra sweets and get back into her normal routine. She is still staying with her family, who are big bakers, so she is concerned that it will be difficult to get back into a routine.

She denies fever, chills, chest pain or shortness of breath, abdominal pain, urinary burning, joint pain or muscle aches. She does have osteoarthritis but denies any joint pain or muscle aches at this time.

She has had atrial fibrillation for many years. She reports that she feels her heart racing only when she is really anxious.

She has been taking protonix 40 mg once daily for reflux and reports that it has been helping.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or urinary burning.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies joint pain or muscle aches.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

• Neck: Thyroid is enlarged but non-tender.
• Cardiovascular: Irregular rate and rhythm.
• Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Elevated blood glucose level. Elevated hemoglobin A1c level.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient is a 52-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of high blood sugar. Her blood glucose level was elevated in the emergency room as well as her hemoglobin A1c level today. We discussed treatment options today including metformin 500 mg twice daily which will help keep her blood sugars down. We also discussed dietary modifications including avoiding foods high in sugar. We will order complete metabolic panel labs to further evaluate for autoimmune disorders which may be contributing to her diabetes mellitus type II diagnosis. The patient will also need to follow up with the nurse today for glucometer education and training on how to perform home glucose monitoring. We will continue metoprolol 25 mg twice daily for atrial fibrillation as tolerated at this time. Protonix 40 mg once daily will continue for reflux symptoms as tolerated at this time.

Due to insurance changes since her last office visit in April 2020, she was switched from Symbicort to Wixela. She also uses Zyrtec in the spring, summer and fall for her seasonal allergy symptoms which tend to work well. She also has known peanut allergy and tolerates almonds and cashews. FAMILY HISTORY: Several family members positive for hypertension.
MEDICATIONS: Benicar HCT 40 mg/25 mg; Amlodipine 10 mg daily.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension; Neurological: Reports palpitations.
VITALS: Blood pressure readings at home: 146-155 mmHg.
PAST HISTORY: Hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY:
ALLERGIES:
The patient presents today with resistant hypertension despite being on three medications at maximum dose. His potassium level was last checked one week ago and was found to be elevated at 4.0 mmol/L. We discussed the possible risks associated with hydrochlorothiazide (his current medication) as well as spironolactone including electrolyte disturbances, dehydration, gynecomastia, dizziness, erectile dysfunction, etc., which are all rare side effects of spironolactone but can occur in some patients. We discussed the American Heart Association website (heart.org) which provides information regarding diet and exercise to help control blood pressure as well as the dash diet plan which is the only eating plan shown to lower blood pressure in randomized controlled trials (RCTs). We also discussed renal denervation as an alternative treatment option for resistant hypertension if needed in the future.
The patient understands all risks associated with these medications and agrees to proceed with treatment today including starting spironolactone at this time due to its effectiveness in lowering aldosterone levels which can cause resistance to other medications such as hydrochlorothiazide which we have already tried without success in this case.
The next step would be carvedilol if the spironolactone does not work after two weeks due to potential side effects such as erectile dysfunction which we discussed today as well as other side effects including electrolyte disturbances such as hypokalemia or hyperkalemia which can occur when taking both hydrochlorothiazide and spironolactone together or gynecomastia which can occur when taking spironolactone alone or both together although this is rare but we discussed this possibility today as well.
The patient will follow up in two weeks for another metabolic panel and blood pressure check while also monitoring potassium levels due to potential electrolyte disturbances from both medications together or from spironolactone alone if needed based on lab results obtained after starting this new medication today.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Return visit for IBS with functional abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant 32-year-old female who was last seen in August of 2019 with flares of abdominal pain, who was diagnosed with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) that was treated with Bentyl. She had a previous prescription for Reglan that she received from the emergency room that she used as needed for nausea. She was instructed to start a low dose fiber supplement, such as Citrucel, daily, probiotics to help with gas and bloating, Bentyl up to four times daily for intestinal cramping, and stop Reglan and use Zofran as needed. Neuromodulators such as Elavil and Buspar were discussed but not started.

Brittany Edwards reports that she has been going out to eat some on Friday nights and Saturday nights and that she has had some spicy foods or shrimp. She notes that her gut probably does not always appreciate that. She has been experiencing both lower belly cramps and upper belly nausea. She notes that her bowel movements have increased from 2-3 times per day to more than 3 times per day since starting the new diet. She notes that she tends to have more diarrhea after eating at Friday's restaurant where they serve pasta with alfredo sauce. She notes that she usually avoids fried chicken but today had some which did not bother her. When asked about alcohol consumption, she states that most of the time it is either tequila or dark liquor; however, if she gets brown liquor, she only drinks two glasses. Occasionally she will drink a martini.

She reports no tenderness in her abdomen but states it is soft and non-tender without any masses or organomegaly.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Abdominal pain: positive.
• Nausea: positive.
• Vomiting: negative.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Abdomen: Soft without tenderness.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Brittany Edwards is a pleasant female with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and functional abdominal pain aggravated by high stress, poor eating habits, and poor sleeping habits.

I have encouraged dietary and lifestyle modifications as well as starting a neuromodulator such as Elavil 25 mg at bedtime for IBS.
She can use Bentyl 20 mg as needed 30-45 minutes prior to eating out at a restaurant. She can also use Zofran if needed. However, I have encouraged her to reduce greasy and fatty foods and alcohol consumption.
We discussed long-term medication options including Elavil which would take effect every night before bedtime.

Follow-up for adult hydrocephalus.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christopher Watson is an 86-year-old male who returns in follow-up for adult hydrocephalus. This is his first visit since undergoing shunt surgery on August 1st, 2020.

Prior to surgery, he was having progressive problems that affected his walking, thinking, and bladder control. These symptoms have improved since the shunt surgery. He now walks to the dining room without assistance and has improved bladder control but still wears diapers. He does not experience headaches or pain where the shunt is located and denies any abdominal pain.

The patient reports that he feels better cognitively and can have a normal conversation with someone now.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Normal.
• Fever: Negative.
• Weight loss: Negative.
• Urinary incontinence: Positive; wearing diapers.
• Genital sores: Negative.
• Decreased or painful output: Negative.
• Neurological: Continued walking impairment and cognitive impairment. No headaches, recent falls, or hallucinations noted today. 
• Psychiatric: Negative for depression, excessive worrying, or mood swings.
