note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hypertension.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Amanda Taylor is a 72-year-old female who presents for follow-up of hypertension. She reports that she has been drinking alcohol 4 to 5 days per week to excess. She denies tobacco use and substance abuse. Her last drink was on Monday. She has been abstinent for 2 days. She has a history of significant alcohol use disorder and myocardial infarction (MI) - mild hypercholesterolemia. At her last visit on April 16th, her blood pressure was 130 over 90. After presenting at 150 over 100, she was prescribed hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg by mouth once daily, and lisinopril 20 mg by mouth once daily.

The patient reports that she is taking her blood pressure medications but only takes half of the lisinopril dose due to lethargy and headaches in the past. She notes that she feels much better since taking the half dose and does not have headaches or swooshing in her left ear anymore.

She reports that she is doing home blood pressure checks at least twice a day, with lower numbers in the morning than in the evening, where she runs anywhere from like 130 to 145 over 95 to 100 on the bottom. However, if she sits for a while and then takes it, it goes down. In the evenings, if she sits there for a while and then takes it, it goes down.

She also notes that she is taking her medicine in the morning when she gets up instead of in the evening.

The patient denies fever, cough, shortness of breath or sore throat.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: No chest tightness or pressure or shortness of breath.
Neurological: No headache.
Psychiatric: Denies anxiety.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Unlabored breathing; cardiac rhythm regular; no murmurs; no gallops; jvp flat.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Alcohol use disorder.
Lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide are currently being taken as prescribed but only half of lisinopril dose due to lethargy and headaches in the past. The patient would like to start naltrexone which we have previously discussed today. We reviewed side effects and risks today including nausea, headache, dizziness, anxiety, tiredness and trouble sleeping but generally these side effects are mild and should go away within a few days.
We discussed potential benefits of alcohol cessation including improvement in hypertension with cessation of alcohol as well as improvement in overall health status.
I recommended upgrading influenza vaccination and shingrix which she deferred today.
We will schedule her back week of June 14th which is likely around the time of her second naltrexone injection.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Thomas Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis. The patient reports that his right knee was injected with a steroid injection on 03/04/2021. Since then, he has been experiencing swelling in his right knee and leg. He rates his pain as a 3 out of 10, but typically rates it at 6. The swelling has been present for approximately two months. The patient notes that the swelling was limited to the knee prior to the injection, but now it is present throughout his entire leg. He has been wearing compression socks frequently, but they have not helped with the swelling. He notes that he has slowed down due to the pain and swelling, and that he finds some activities too fast. When he is sitting for a long period of time and then tries to get up, he experiences stiffness and needs to use a cane to get his bearings. After a few minutes, the stiffness subsides.

The patient reports that he has been taking his medications regularly. He is currently taking Xeljanz XR 11 mg daily and Celebrex 200 mg daily.

The patient denies any recent trauma or injury.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Rheumatoid arthritis.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports that he enjoys salty snacks.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain and swelling.
Neurological: Reports stiffness when getting up from sitting.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals mild effusion around the joint with some pitting edema in the ankle region. There is warmth over the right knee.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
None available.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Thomas Nelson is a 72-year-old male who presents today for ongoing management of rheumatoid arthritis.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's current symptoms are consistent with worsening rheumatoid arthritis after receiving a steroid injection in his right knee on 03/04/2021. His current symptoms include increased pain, swelling, stiffness, and decreased range of motion in his right knee as well as generalized edema throughout his entire leg.
- Medical Treatment Plan: We discussed treatment options today including additional steroid injections and x-rays to evaluate for possible fluid accumulation in the joint as well as physical therapy to help improve function and reduce pain. We also discussed dietary modifications such as reducing salt intake which can help reduce fluid retention leading to edema.
- Patient Education: I advised him on dietary modifications such as reducing salt intake which can help reduce fluid retention leading to edema. I also advised him on elevating his legs when possible especially at night time.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with all recommended medical treatment plans.

Jacqueline Miller is a 40-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of perioral dermatitis. She reports that she has been using doxycycline cream twice daily for the past two weeks, but has noticed that her rash has plateaued and is not continuing to improve. She discontinued breastfeeding and started taking doxycycline at that time. She was prescribed MetroCream and sulfacetamide wash by her dermatologist, but stopped using MetroCream because she was worried about the side effects. She has been using the sulfacetamide wash twice daily, but notes that it is drying out her skin. The patient denies any other lotions or moisturizers.

The patient reports that she has been experiencing ocular rosacea as well. She notes that she is sun sensitive whenever she goes outside and uses sunscreen to protect herself from sunburn.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Skin: Reports erythematous papules on bilateral medial cheeks.
• Eyes: Reports ocular rosacea.
note.objective_exam:

Fitzpatrick skin type IV.
• Skin: Erythematous papules on bilateral medial cheeks.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Jacqueline Miller is a 40-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of perioral dermatitis and ocular rosacea.
• Medical Reasoning: Perioral dermatitis is a common inflammatory condition of the face, typically occurring around the mouth. It can be caused by a variety of factors including hormonal changes, acne vulgaris, or topical irritants such as cosmetics or soaps. note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michael Rodriguez is a pleasant 47-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right upper quadrant abdominal pain. The onset of his pain began several weeks ago and has been intermittent. He describes the pain as a squeezing severe pain that comes and goes, but when it does come it is really severe. He rates his pain an 8 on a scale of 0 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain he has ever experienced. The patient states that the pain is located right underneath his ribs on the right side of his abdomen. He reports that the pain is related to eating and occurs immediately after eating or a couple of hours later. The patient denies any nausea or vomiting.

The patient reports that he was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes approximately 3 months ago and has been managing it with diet and exercise. He notes that he has cut back on sugar and started a keto diet which has resulted in weight loss of approximately 25 pounds. He notes that since starting this diet, his blood sugars have improved but he still experiences right upper quadrant abdominal pain.

The patient reports that both his mother and father had gallbladder disease and had to have their gallbladders removed.

The patient denies fevers but does report low grade fevers when the pain is severe.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fevers.
• Gastrointestinal: Reports nausea, vomiting.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, gallops, or rubs.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Gastrointestinal: Soft non-distended abdomen with positive bowel sounds.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound obtained at an outside facility shows multiple gallstones present in the gallbladder with some mild thickening. The common bile duct size is within normal limits at 4.1 mm.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michael Rodriguez is a pleasant 47-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
I do believe you have some mild cholecystitis with gallstones I do not appreciate any frank obstruction but it looks like your gallbladder is inflamed and it looks like that's happened maybe over the last few weeks since you've been having those symptoms.
Since you have not had any improvement with dietary modifications I am going to make the recommendation that we do remove your gallbladder and I would like to perform a laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
The surgery will take about an hour to an hour and a half and you'll probably spend the night in the hospital because we just want to monitor you post procedure to make sure everything is okay. You will still want to avoid those high fat foods after surgery and eat foods that are going to be high in fiber.
Do you have any questions about what our assessment and plan is for this?
The other thing I want to talk briefly about is now your not your type two diabetes I want you to follow up with your physician just to make sure that you're handling your diabetes especially the fact that you're going to have surgery and those type of things and we will just continue to monitor your diabetes as has been outlined by your additional either your endocrinologist or your primary care provider.
The nurse will come in today get some paperwork signed if you don't have any questions for me we will see you next week then we will get this gallbladder out.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right shoulder pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a 67-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right shoulder pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 4 days ago when he was tackled while playing tackle football. He denies any numbness or tingling in his fingers, but reports that his strength is slightly diminished in his right arm. He notes that he has been avoiding lifting anything heavy due to the pain. The patient reports that he has been taking Tylenol for the pain, but it has not helped at all. He denies any neck problems, and reports that his elbow, wrist, and other joints are all doing well.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right shoulder pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in his fingers.
Cardiovascular: Reports a slight headache.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cervical Spine: No tenderness to palpation of the cervical spine. Full range of motion on head exam. No ecchymosis or bruising.
Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of the posterior shoulder at the acromioclavicular joint. Decreased abduction and adduction to about 90 degrees only. Pain with supination and pronation of the right arm. Palpable radial artery pulse.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right shoulder reveals an acute acromioclavicular joint fracture.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

For Matthew Allen's right shoulder injury for acute acromioclavicular joint fracture, I have placed him in a sling for now. We will prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once a day to help with pain management. We will order a CT scan of his right shoulder just to get a better look at how the joint looks. We will refer him to physical therapy to strengthen his shoulder in hopes of avoiding surgery in the future.

Patient Agreements.
Patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Lower back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jeremy Adams is a 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of lower back pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 4 months ago when he was moving some boxes when his son was moving out of his college dorm. He states that he felt a “tweak” in his lower back at that time and has been experiencing low back pain ever since. He denies fevers or chills. He also reports right foot tingling, which resolved after about an hour. He denies bowel issues and bladder issues. The patient reports that he is able to carry heavy objects without difficulty, but feels the sensation so he is a little nervous about carrying something heavy.

The patient has been taking Tylenol and ibuprofen for pain management, but notes that the ibuprofen seems to be better than Tylenol for a shorter period of time. He denies any stomach upset from the ibuprofen.

The patient has tried heat and ice for pain management, but notes that nothing seems to help.

The patient has seen an urgent care center and they wanted him to do an MRI, but he was concerned because they maxed out his insurance so he did not do it at that time. However, because it has been going on for so long, he is concerned now and would like to move forward with the MRI.

The patient had right knee surgery 2 years ago in spring of 2020. He states that his right knee feels 95% improved since the surgery.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fevers or chills.
• Musculoskeletal: Reports lower back pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No bony protuberance noted.
Lumbar Spine: Decreased flexion and extension of the lower back. Positive straight leg raise.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-rays of the lumbar spine were obtained today and reviewed by me in office today. There were no acute bony abnormalities noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Jeremy Adams is a 57-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of lower back pain.
I do believe it sounds like you have an acute disk herniation based on your history today. This did happen a few months ago but it sounds like that’s what you had based on the fact that you’re still having symptoms.
I do want to go ahead and order a lumbar spine MRI to get a better look at what’s going on today. We’ll also continue with physical therapy as well as prescribe meloxicam fifteen milligrams once daily to help with your pain management today.
If we do end up having an MRI we can discuss other treatment options such as epidural steroid injections which may help take down some of that inflammation.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Scott Miller is a 36-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 3 days ago when he was playing pickup soccer and felt a pop in his right knee. He notes that his right knee is swollen, but the swelling has decreased. He reports that his knee feels limited in motion and that he is unable to bear weight on it or walk on it at all. His gait reveals a marked limp on his right leg.

Examination of the right knee reveals effusion and ecchymosis. There is tenderness to palpation over the medial joint line.
Range of motion testing reveals significant effusion in the right knee, slight ecchymosis, positive Lachman's test, and lack of terminal extension to about 115 degrees as well as lack of terminal flexion secondary to pain.
Neurovascularly, bilateral lower extremities are intact.
Muscle strength testing reveals grade 5 out of 5 bilaterally.

Based on my examination today, Scott Miller's right knee injury is suggestive of an anterior cruciate ligament tear (ACL tear). We will order an MRI today to evaluate for ACL integrity. In the meantime, I have prescribed meloxicam 5 mg daily for anti-inflammatory effects and pain relief. I have also recommended ice if needed for swelling and pain relief. Scott will need to limit activities until we receive results from his MRI; this includes limiting work activities as well as jogging until we can discuss further options with him after reviewing results from MRI.

Patient Agreements Obtained.

Elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Teresa Sullivan is a 33-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 4 days ago when she was working on pottery. She has been creating pottery for her son's birthday and has been working on a ceramic bowl with full decorations. She reports that she has been working on this project very intensely and that the pain has been worsening. She notes that she is unable to work on this project due to the pain. She denies any history of trauma to her elbow, but does report that she has had hypertension and diabetes type 2 for many years.

The patient reports that her blood pressure is in the 110s to 130s range and her blood sugar levels are from 150 to 170 mg/dL. She takes lisinopril 10 mg daily and metformin 500 mg twice daily.

She reports that she has been taking ibuprofen, but it is not helping with her pain. She tried ice initially, but it did not help.

Pain level: 7/10 at its worst.

The patient reports that the pain radiates down her arm and along the medial aspect of her arm.

She denies any radiation into her shoulder or neck.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No tenderness or erythema noted in the cervical region.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.
Pulse: Appropriate rate and rhythm.
Cardiovascular: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard upon auscultation of heart.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of right elbow was reviewed today by Dr. Smith who notes no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Teresa Sullivan is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right elbow pain consistent with medial epicondylitis. The onset of symptoms began approximately 4 days ago when she was working on pottery. She has been creating pottery for her son's birthday and has been working on a ceramic bowl with full decorations. She reports that she has been working on this project very intensely and that the pain has been worsening. She notes that she is unable to work on this project due to the pain.

Medical Reasoning:
The patient’s x-ray was reviewed by Dr. Smith who notes no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality so we can rule out a fracture as a cause for her symptoms today. Her symptoms are consistent with medial epicondylitis which is an overuse injury caused by damage to tendons in the arm.
Medical Treatment:
The patient will rest her right arm while wearing a sling while awake today as well as apply ice to her elbow for twenty minutes three times per day until further notice. We will also prescribe ibuprofen at six hundred milligrams every six hours with food until further notice as well.
Patient Agreements:
The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan today.

Right heel pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right heel pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the lower extremities reveals tenderness to palpation over the right Achilles tendon.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Dennis Martin is a 46-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right heel pain.

Diagnosis: Achilles tendinitis.
Medical Reasoning: This is from overuse when we see this frequently when somebody starts to get in and train aggressively for an event.
Medical Treatment Plan: I have recommended that he discontinue training for a week or two until this heals before we move into that next phase. I did not ask him about medication but I'm assuming whatever he was doing wasn't working significantly so I would like him to take ibuprofen or Advil that's the same medication and take three tablets every six hours to help with inflammation around his Achilles tendon. We will also order two physical therapy visits to help strengthen his lower extremities as well as provide stretching knowledge. We will follow up with him within a week to ten days following his first couple physical therapy appointments to monitor how he is doing.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Non-healing right foot ulcer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer. The patient reports that she has had this ulcer for approximately 1 year. She notes that she initially had a little blister on her right foot, which she picked at and it became infected. She then went to her primary care provider (PCP) who prescribed antibiotics, which seemed to help initially. However, the ulcer has not healed and she has been taking Keflex for the past 5 months. She denies any trauma to her foot and denies any pain. She does note that she has neuropathy secondary to her diabetes.

The patient also reports that she has been feeling more tired lately and has noticed an increase in drainage from the ulcer.

The patient denies fevers or chills.

She reports that she will be walking around at the zoo this weekend with her family and eating out as well.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fatigue.
• Musculoskeletal: Pain.
• Neurological: Decreased sensation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

CV: No murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard.
Respiratory: No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi appreciated.
Cardiovascular: No edema in lower extremities noted.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right foot reveals a 1 by 2 centimeter 2 inch circular wound on the dorsal aspect of the lateral right foot proximal to the fifth metatarsophalangeal joint. There is minimal granulation tissue present with yellow slough. There is no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there is no evidence of fluid collection. There is no evidence of necrosis or bony exposure.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right foot was performed today and revealed no evidence of osteomyelitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Christina Cooper is a 77-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of a non-healing right foot ulcer secondary to diabetic neuropathy. The patient’s last hemoglobin A1C was 10%. Today’s examination revealed a diabetic foot ulcer on her right foot with minimal granulation tissue present with yellow sloughing. There was no surrounding erythema or cellulitis and there was no evidence of fluid collection or necrosis around it. There was no odor present and there was no bony exposure noted upon examination today.

I have reviewed today’s x-ray which revealed no evidence of osteomyelitis which is good news as we can continue trying to heal this wound without surgical intervention at this time. We will continue with debridement in office today followed by colagenase ointment applied once daily until we see improvement in size of wound. We will follow up in 2 weeks at which point we may perform another debridement if needed.
We will also order an ABI (ankle brachial index) to determine if there is adequate blood flow to this area so we can try other goals for healing if needed.
The patient will be fitted for a surgical shoe today as well.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up after an interior STEMI.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Julia Anderson is a 74-year-old female who presents for follow-up after an interior STEMI where she required another stent placement. She reports that she was experiencing similar symptoms to her last heart attack, including chest pain that would not go away. She went to the emergency room and was told that she needed another stent. She denies any chest pain or shortness of breath. She has been able to exercise at all since her last visit with the exception of walking her dog daily.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Coronary artery disease, hypertension, diabetes.
Surgical: RCA stent placement in 2018.
SOCIAL HISTORY

Patient reports that she walks her dog daily and enjoys pizza and tries (a type of food).
MEDICATIONS

Patient reports that she is taking aspirin 81 mg daily; Brilinta 90 mg twice daily; Lipitor 80 mg daily; Toprol 50 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; metformin.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base. No carotid bruits appreciated.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
Gastrointestinal: Edema swelling in the lower extremities with pitting edema on the right radial artery.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

EKG shows normal sinus rhythm, good R wave progression, evolutionary changes anticipated after STEMI.
Echocardiogram shows reduced ejection fraction of 35%.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Primary diagnosis is coronary artery disease. We will continue aspirin 81 mg daily and Brilinta 90 mg twice daily. We will continue Lipitor at a high dose of 80 mg daily and Toprol at a dose of 50 mg daily. We will refer her to cardiac rehab so we can get some education and give her some confidence to get back to exercising regularly. I think most patients who have been through cardiac rehab do pretty well for this reason.
Second diagnosis is newly reduced left ventricular dysfunction and moderate mitral regurgitation. I think this means that your heart is pumping a bit concerning but I think given your history it will improve over time. We got you into the cath lab pretty quickly so I think that the muscle is just kinda stunned like surprised and since you are compliant with your meds I think you will recover. We are going to continue lisinopril at a dose of twenty milligrams daily however considering that you are retaining fluid I think that your third diagnosis is acute heart failure which we are going to prescribe Lasix at a dose of forty milligrams once a day and Aldactone at twelve point five milligrams once a day as well as repeat an echo in about two months last but not least there is hypertension which seems fine with aldactone but we do want to maybe get you into some nutrition counseling to consider what other diet options might be available to you maybe suggestions of things that you haven't thought about like cutting out meat especially any kind of preserved meat like pepperoni but maybe finding you some alternatives how does that sound?
The patient understands and agrees with this plan.

Medications.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jose Thompson is a 75-year-old male who presents today for a follow-up visit. The patient reports that he is doing okay, but he is concerned about all the medications that he is taking. He has been on aspirin, Brilinta, fish oil, Crestor, and Metoprolol 50 mg once a day since his heart attack 6 months ago. He denies taking the Crestor at this time.

The patient reports that when he stands up quickly he gets dizzy. He denies chest pain or shortness of breath with exertion.

The patient reports that his A1c was close to 60% and that his fasting glucose was in the low 130s.

The patient states that he had diabetes prior to his heart attack and had not seen a dietitian yet.

PAST HISTORY
Medical: History of coronary artery disease and diabetes mellitus.
Surgical: Stent placement at the left anterior descending artery.
SOCIAL HISTORY: Lives with his dog; San Francisco 49ers fan.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neck: No jugular venous distention or carotid bruits heard on exam.
Cardiovascular: Grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Coronary artery disease:
The patient continues to take aspirin, Brilinta, fish oil, Crestor (40 mg once daily), and Metoprolol 50 mg once daily. His most recent hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 16%. We discussed this today and reviewed dietary modifications as well as additional referrals for cardiac rehabilitation. I have referred him for cardiac rehabilitation today as well as ordered another hemoglobin A1c test today due to elevated levels from last visit. I have also ordered another referral for diabetic education due to elevated fasting glucose levels from last visit. We discussed insulin therapy again today but we will need to discuss this further with his primary care physician before proceeding with insulin therapy at this time. I have also placed refills on all of these medications today in addition to prescribing him Metoprolol again due to continued symptoms of dizziness upon standing up quickly which may be related to medication side effects or possibly related to coronary artery disease itself given his history of heart attack six months ago.
Stage three chronic kidney disease:
The patient’s creatinine levels were stable after undergoing contrast dye imaging yesterday however we discussed this further today and we will need to schedule an appointment with Dr Miller for further evaluation given stage three chronic kidney disease status based on creatinine levels from yesterday’s imaging study which were elevated compared to previous labs without contrast dye exposure in order for us to determine if there are any additional steps needed moving forward such as dialysis or other interventions such as medication adjustments etc...
Diabetes mellitus:
The most recent hemoglobin A1c was elevated at 16%. We reviewed dietary modifications again today along with additional referrals for diabetic education in order for him to better manage his diabetes moving forward.

Right hand numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling. Musculoskeletal: Reports right hand numbness and tingling.
Neurological: Reports right hand pain.
note.objective_exam:

note.assessment_and_plan:

Alexis Gutierrez is a 33-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of right hand numbness and tingling.

I have reviewed her EMG results today, which revealed thickening in the membranes of her wrist consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome. We discussed conservative treatment options today including a wrist splint to wear at night, ibuprofen up to 600 mg four times daily, and physical therapy if needed. We discussed surgical options as well if conservative treatment fails.

Patient Agreements.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

George Young is a 59-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow pain. The onset of his symptoms began approximately 1 week ago when he was playing lacrosse with his children. He reports that he was throwing the ball and suddenly started experiencing right elbow pain. He denies any history of falling, but believes that he may have been hit by his son during play. The patient states that the pain is sharp and occurs anytime he moves his right elbow. The patient reports that the pain radiates down to his forearm. He has tried taking Advil for pain relief, but has not been consistent with this treatment.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Hypertension, Diabetes.
Social: Plays lacrosse with his children.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Lisinopril 20 mg daily; Metformin 500 mg daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No cervical spine tenderness or rigidity.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border, otherwise normal heart exam.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right elbow obtained today shows no fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

George Young is a 59-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right elbow contusion. I have reviewed his x-ray today which was normal without any fractures or bony abnormalities. His blood pressure today was 150/90 mmHg which is elevated and higher than usual. We discussed this with him and I explained that it could be due to white coat hypertension as I also experience this myself. We discussed dietary modifications and he reported that he has been compliant with a low salt diet during the pandemic which is good to hear. We also discussed diabetes management and we will continue him on metformin 500 mg daily as prescribed, however we will obtain an A1c today to check his glucose levels and see if we need to adjust his medication in the future.

For today's treatment plan, I have prescribed him ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain relief as well as ice therapy three times a day for twenty minutes at a time to help reduce swelling and pain in his right elbow. We discussed limiting lacrosse play until further improvement is seen in order to allow healing time.

Patient Agreements Obtained.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Hospital follow-up after acute on chronic CHF exacerbation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

James Davis is an 82-year-old male who presents for hospital follow-up after an acute on chronic CHF exacerbation. The patient reports that he was doing well until he noticed his ankles were swelling. He then experienced shortness of breath and called 911. When the paramedics arrived, they placed him on a special mask to breathe. He was subsequently admitted to the hospital where his blood pressure was noted. The patient reports that he has been taking his medications most times, but sometimes misses a dose or two. He does acknowledge that he has been watching his diet, but admits to having some slips.

The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or problems sleeping since he has been home.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports shortness of breath.
Respiratory: Denies dyspnea.
Gastrointestinal: Reports edema in the lower extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Blood pressure 128/72 mmHg; heart rate 79 bpm; respiratory rate 26; SpO2 99% on room air.
NECK: No jugular venous distension.
HEART: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur which is stable.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Echocardiogram shows preserved EF of 55%, abnormal diastolic filling, and mild to moderate mitral regurgitation.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Congestive heart failure.
- Medical Reasoning: This appears to be caused by dietary indiscretion and uncontrolled hypertension.
- Medical Treatment: Continue bumex 2 mg once daily as prescribed. Continue to watch diet and avoid salty foods. We will continue monitoring for any signs of worsening heart failure with weight gain greater than three pounds in two days. We will also order a renal artery ultrasound today to rule out any secondary causes of kidney disease.
- Patient Education and Counseling: We discussed the importance of watching diet and avoiding salty foods as well as the importance of weight monitoring.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan today.

The patient enjoys playing soccer for the community league.

No known drug allergies.

note.objective_results:
RESULTS
Right ankle x-ray: No fracture.
note.assessment_and_plan:

Gregory Hernandez is a pleasant 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain.

I have also recommended that he continue to elevate his leg when seated and ice it as needed for pain relief. Additionally, I have recommended that he wear an Aircast brace for stabilization of the ankle for the next 1-2 days and then start walking on it as tolerated.
We discussed that his symptoms should significantly improve in 2 weeks at which point we will re-evaluate him at that time.
INSTRUCTIONS
Continue to elevate your leg when seated and ice it as needed for pain relief. Continue taking NSAIDs as needed for any associated pain.
We will follow up with you then to assess how you are doing.

Chest pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Elizabeth Scott is a 53-year-old female today complaining of chest pain. She has a past medical history of diabetes type 2 and high blood pressure. She denies chest pain at this time, but reports that she experiences pressure and dull chest pain when she starts walking. The onset of her symptoms began approximately 3 months ago. She denies any exacerbating or relieving factors. Her blood sugars have been elevated due to lack of activity and diet changes.

She denies shortness of breath, sweating, or clamminess at this time.

PAST HISTORY

Medical: Diabetes type 2.
Family History: Heart disease.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: No jugular venous distention. No carotid bruits.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Regular rate and rhythm. No murmurs, gallops, or rubs heard otherwise.
Musculoskeletal: Soft abdomen without tenderness or guarding. No masses appreciated in the abdomen or back exam.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

EKG obtained today was normal.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elizabeth Scott is a 53-year-old female today who presents for evaluation of chest pain.
- Chest pain is likely due to unstable angina secondary to her history of diabetes and suspected history of hypertension as well as her family history of heart disease. We reviewed her EKG today which was normal so we do not see signs of a heart attack at this time. We will refer her to cardiology for further evaluation and management.
- Her blood sugars have been elevated due to lack of activity and diet changes so we will continue with the metformin 500 mg twice daily as prescribed but we will also schedule an eye exam with ophthalmology for diabetic retinopathy screening as well as order another hemoglobin A1c today.
- Her blood pressure has been trending high over the last few years so we will start her on hydrochlorothiazide in addition to monitoring her blood pressure at home with a home blood pressure cuff using Epic MyChart daily in the morning when she wakes up for the next two weeks until we can review the results together in clinic again at that time we can discuss any necessary adjustments to her medications if needed based on how things are going at home with monitoring her blood pressure daily in addition to reviewing her hemoglobin A1c results from today's visit as well as reviewing any additional findings from our EKG today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Bilateral knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sophia Jackson is a 30-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of bilateral knee pain. The onset of her pain began approximately 6 months ago and she denies any specific injury that may have caused her pain. She describes the pain as deep achy and she hears creaking in her knees. She notes that her pain is worse when getting from a seated position to standing, after watching TV, and going up and down stairs. She notes that resting for some time does help with her pain. She has tried icing, wrapping with an ace bandage, and taking ibuprofen or Aleve but she tries to avoid taking any medications. She reports that she used to run 5-6 miles a day but now she can only get to half a mile before her leg starts hurting.

SOCIAL HISTORY

The patient reports that she works from home and runs outside during the winter.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports bilateral knee pain.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Normal.
NEURO: Patellar reflexes are symmetrical bilaterally.
MSK: Examination of the lower extremities reveals normal gait.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-rays of bilateral knees were obtained today and reviewed by me. There are no fractures or osteoarthritis noted.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

For bilateral knee pain, based on what the patient told me today, her exam, and reviewing her x-rays today, I have reviewed the literature and believe this is consistent with patellofemoral pain syndrome. This is a very common condition that we see in active young people that causes knee pain. We discussed treatment options today including continued use of ibuprofen or anti-inflammatory as needed to help with the pain as well as physical therapy where they will show you a number of lower extremity exercises which will help increase your lower extremity strength, mobility, and correct any incorrect running mechanics that you may have. We discussed goals for treatment today including getting back into running again but we will continue to assess your progress at each visit.
INSTRUCTIONS
The patient understands.

• Chest pain: No.
• Shortness of breath: No.
• Nasal congestion: Yes.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Alan Butler is a 61-year-old male who presents today with complaints of shortness of breath. The onset began over the weekend after he took a very long bike ride, approximately 3 hours. He reports that he was very light-headed and short of breath. He denies chest pain, fever, or any other symptoms. He notes that his vision has been great since his cataract surgery 4.5 months ago.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Reports fevers.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath.
• Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain.
• Gastrointestinal: Denies abdominal pain or nausea/vomiting.
• Neurological: Reports headaches.
• Musculoskeletal: Denies lower extremity edema.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: Supple without jugular venous distension.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
Respiratory: Litttle wheezes expiratory bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Pulmonary function test was within normal limits. Chest x-ray obtained today is normal with no pulmonary edema or pneumonia. CBC was within normal limits.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Today, Alan Butler is a 61-year-old male who presents today with complaints of shortness of breath. His examination reveals supple neck without jugular venous distension and regular rate and rhythm without murmurs in the heart exam. Litttle wheezes expiratory bilaterally were appreciated in the respiratory exam. His pulmonary function test was within normal limits and his chest x-ray obtained today is normal with no pulmonary edema or pneumonia. His CBC was within normal limits as well.

His current symptoms are consistent with an asthma exacerbation from exercising and allergies, so I have prescribed him albuterol inhaler, two puffs every four hours as needed for wheezing or for shortness of breath today. I have also ordered a pulmonary referral for him to follow up with tomorrow due to his current symptoms.

Regarding his reflux, everything seems stable and we will continue on Protonix as needed for reflux today. We will continue imitrex as needed for migraines as well.

She has been so tired and exhausted that she has not been able to keep up with her exercise routine. She denies any blood in her stools or dark stools. She denies spotting with her periods. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, body aches or weight loss.

• Constitutional: Fatigue.
• Cardiovascular: Dyspnea on exertion.
• Respiratory: Shortness of breath.
• Gastrointestinal: Constipation.
note.objective_exam:

Cardiovascular: Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border. No murmurs heard elsewhere.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Gastrointestinal: Tenderness to palpation in right lower quadrant.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Hemoglobin A1c is 8.2; Labs are within normal limits; Anemia labs are pending.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Abnormal lab findings.
• Medical Reasoning: The patient's hemoglobin level is low at 8.2 and should be greater than 13-14 g/dL for a female of her age and race.
• Medical Treatment: We need to investigate why it is low. I will order endoscopy and colonoscopy to rule out gastrointestinal bleeding from inside the belly. We will also need to order anemia labs to determine the type of anemia she may have.
• Patient Education and Counseling: I advised the patient that we will need further workup before we can determine what type of anemia she may have and what treatment options are available for her at this time.
• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

James Moore is a 57-year-old male who presents today with joint pain. The patient reports that he has been putting a few more miles on the bike each day and that his knees have been killing him, just more so in the last 3-4 days. The patient states that it is bilateral and that it usually hurts more in the morning when he wakes up, but by the end of the day, he starts to feel that same sensation around dinner time. He denies any swelling or redness of his knees. He denies any other associated fatigue or fever.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Denies chest pain or shortness of breath.
Musculoskeletal: Reports joint pain in both knees.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Auscultation of heart reveals a 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, which we have heard in the past. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the knees reveals bilateral edema and slight erythema. There is a slight effusion present on the right knee. Pain to palpation of the right knee. Decreased range of motion bilaterally.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was obtained today and reviewed by me today. There is no bony abnormality present, no fracture present, which is not surprising based on history.
Electrocardiogram was stable in comparison to last year.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Joint pain.
- Medical Reasoning: I am concerned that this may be from a flareup of his lupus.
- Patient Education: I explained to him that we will need to order an autoimmune panel to see where we stand.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an autoimmune panel today.
2. Coronary artery disease.
- Medical Reasoning: He has been doing well with his current medications and ekg looks good today.
- Patient Education: I explained to him that we will need to order a lipid panel and another echocardiogram today.
- Medical Treatment: We will order an echocardiogram today.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient is a 75-year-old female who presents for a follow-up visit today. Her current medications include lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide 20/25 mg tablet, take 1 tablet daily; metoprolol 50 mg tablet, take 1 tablet daily; amlodipine 10 mg tablet, take 1 tablet daily; atorvastatin tablet; metformin; glimepiride 4 mg tablet, take 2 tablets by oral route twice per day.
Her hemoglobin A1C was elevated at 9.9% last time. We discussed this with the patient and we want her to increase the glimepiride from two milligrams twice per day to four milligrams twice per day starting today with the new prescription that I will write for her today. We discussed that she should watch for low sugars which include weakness, shakiness, sweating and notify us if this occurs.
The patient’s blood pressure was elevated at home last week but it is better now so we will continue the combination of medications including lisinopril/hydrochlorothiazide and metoprolol as prescribed today.
The patient’s cholesterol is high and she has peripheral vascular disease with neuropathy in her legs so we really want to keep her on the high dose of atorvastatin or Lipitor to protect the arteries so we will continue this medication as prescribed today as well.
The patient continues to smoke despite our previous discussions regarding smoking cessation so we will continue our previous plan of quitting smoking which includes counseling and nicotine replacement therapy (NRT).
The patient’s vision has improved after cataract surgery however she prefers the other lens over this one because it is funny looking so we will discuss options for cleaning up the eye with laser treatment if needed during our next visit.
The patient’s extremities are without edema and pulses are palpable on dorsalis pedis posterior tibial. She has thickened nails which were noted during examination today as well as mildly dry skin without any skin breakdowns noted today. Mildly decreased sensation in tips of first and second toes were also noted during examination today.
We discussed all of these findings with the patient today and reviewed all current medications including side effects as well as any questions she may have had regarding them.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Evaluation of numbness and tingling.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Elijah Cook is a 60-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of numbness and tingling in his hands. The onset of these symptoms began approximately 3 weeks ago, after he sustained a motor vehicle accident in December 2019 resulting in broken wrists. He states that the numbness and tingling have been progressively worsening over the last month. The patient reports that the right wrist is more affected than the left, but both have gotten worse. He notes that he wears a splint on his right wrist, but not on his left. The patient also reports mild neck stiffness, which he attributes to a contusion from the motor vehicle accident.

The patient describes the numbness and tingling as occurring on both sides of his hands, starting from his middle and ring fingers up to about his elbow. He notes that they are more noticeable at night and throughout the day, but they come and go. The patient denies any loss of sensation in his hands or fingers.

The patient reports that he has been taking nerve pain medicine prescribed by his primary care provider, but has not been consistent with taking it as prescribed.

The patient denies any history of thyroid issues.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Constitutional: Fatigue, weight gain.
GI: Excessive appetite, bloating.
Eyes: Floaters.
Cardiovascular: Shortness of breath, leg swelling.
Endocrine: Always hungry.
Skin: Dryness, itching.
Musculoskeletal: Gout, muscle pain.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological:
- Sensation: Normal except for diminished pinprick sensation in third and fourth fingers on the right hand. Decreased sensation in fourth and fifth fingers on the left hand.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Elijah Cook is a 60-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of numbness and tingling in his hands. He states that the numbness and tingling have been progressively worsening over the last month. He notes that he wears a splint on his right wrist but not on his left hand. The patient also reports mild neck stiffness which he attributes to a contusion from this motor vehicle accident.
I am concerned for bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome or potentially bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome based on his symptom presentation today; however, I believe this to be bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome due to nerve irritation secondary to past trauma to these areas causing pain and tingling as described by him today.
The plan includes scheduling an EMG test today to further evaluate for carpal tunnel syndrome or cubital tunnel syndrome. After reviewing all test results we will discuss additional treatment options including possible injections or surgery referral if needed.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up of constipation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Michelle King is a 39-year-old female who presents today for a follow-up of constipation. The patient was admitted to district regional hospital on 06/29/2021, and was discharged on 07/02/2021. She was experiencing increasing concerns for spasms and lightheadedness, significant constipation, and reported diaphoresis. She was evaluated in the emergency department where she was febrile and had significantly elevated white blood cell count of 23,000. There were concerns for ongoing urinary tract infection, but she was treated with IV antibiotic therapy. She had labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. In the end, she slowly improved. She does have a supra-pubic catheter.

The patient reports that her hospitalization was more likely due to her dysreflexia from her quadriplegia that typically occurs. She did have a lot of vital signs changes including blood pressure fluctuations.

The patient feels like she has a good bowel regimen including taking the miralax regularly as a primary treatment for constipation issues as well as lactulose for severe constipation. She feels like this was less likely a true urinary tract infection and was just related to her constipation.

She also reports that she is unvaccinated against COVID-19 due to hesitations regarding side effects.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Fever.
• Cardiovascular: Hypertension.
• Neurological: Lightheadedness.
• Musculoskeletal: Constipation.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

No pain or discomfort noted.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Suprapubic catheter.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Michelle King is a 39-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of acute to chronic constipation secondary to dysreflexia from quadriplegia status post spinal cord injury.
• Medical Reasoning:
- The patient’s hospitalization may have been more likely due to her dysreflexia from her quadriplegia status post spinal cord injury rather than an underlying urinary tract infection as she did not have any symptoms consistent with UTI such as fever or leukocytosis.
- Her leukocytosis may be related to dehydration secondary to constipation which can lead to further inflammation in the bowel.
- Her hypertension may be related to dehydration secondary to constipation which can lead to further inflammation in the bowel.
- Her lightheadedness may be related to dehydration secondary to constipation which can lead to further inflammation in the bowel.
- Her headache may be related to dehydration secondary to constipation which can lead to further inflammation in the bowel.
- Her vomiting may be related to dehydration secondary to constipation which can lead to further inflammation in the bowel.
- Her spasms may be related to dehydration secondary to constipation which can lead to further inflammation in the bowel.
• Medical Treatment:
The patient will continue with Miralax as needed for laxation and lactulose as needed for severe constipation. We discussed that this is less likely due an underlying UTI and more likely due her dysreflexia from her quadriplegia status post spinal cord injury. We also discussed that this could be related due dehydration secondary to her chronic constipation issues. We discussed that we should wait until after we see some improvement in her bowel habits before we repeat labs again at this time since it is too soon after discharge from hospitalization. We will repeat fasting labs including CBC in 3 weeks if there are no improvements in bowel habits at that time.

Abdominal pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney. She reports that she has been experiencing some stomach burning. She endorses hesitancy while urinating and she states she has to wait for her urinary flow to commence. She endorses occasional dysuria. Ashley denies hematuria. Some beverages are associated with dysuria, thus the patient drinks mainly water, Gatorade and V8 juice.

The patient plays on softball team and is interested in joining a drill team over the summer.

Patient reports that her paternal grandfather had myocardial infarction, posterior urethral valves, obstructive neuropathy, end stage chronic kidney disease was dialysis dependent, failed renal transplant.

PATIENT HISTORY

The patient is still experiencing some stomach burning. She reports hesitancy while urinating and she states she has to wait for her urinary flow to commence. She endorses occasional dysuria. Ashley denies hematuria. Some beverages are associated with dysuria, thus the patient drinks mainly water, Gatorade and V8 juice.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS:
Pepcid 40 mg once daily.
Claritin as needed for allergies.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Cardiovascular: Lungs and heart sound great.
Gastrointestinal: Well-appearing female, alert and oriented, sitting comfortably on my chair today without acute distress.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Abdominal ultrasound was performed on 03/22/2021 which revealed an atrophic right kidney.
CT abdomen and pelvis was performed on 03/22/2021 which revealed cysts or something on her kidney and ovaries as well as some other places. Her lymph nodes were swollen and they found some infection.
CMP was performed on 03/22/2021.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Ashley James is a 14-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of abnormal renal ultrasound with an atrophic right kidney.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's abdominal pain may be related to her atrophic right kidney which is causing her left kidney to work harder possibly causing the left to appear bigger. We will continue to monitor both kidneys' size as well as their overall function through annual ultrasounds.
- Patient Education: I recommended that we avoid non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines like ibuprofen and opt to use tylenol instead due to the strain it puts on her kidneys during physical activity such as softball or drill team in the summer time. We also discussed the importance of staying well hydrated during these activities by drinking at least two liters per day of water.
- Medical Treatment: We discussed starting a healthy diet and continuing an active lifestyle early in life will help keep her kidneys healthier as an adult. I recommended that we continue monitoring her blood pressure annually due to her increased risk of developing hypertension due to this condition.
- Additional Testing: We will continue monitoring proteinuria through urinalysis annually as well as performing blood pressure checks annually going forward.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands all recommendations provided today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Sean Phillips is a 35-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of left back pain. The onset of his pain began approximately 1 year ago after undergoing lumbar microdiscectomy in November 2020. He reports that he has been taking high-dose gabapentin for severe nerve pain through his back and lower extremities prior to the microdiscectomy. He states that he has been taking ibuprofen 800 mg daily for his pain. The patient reports that his significant other always tells him to stretch and it always helps, but stretching does not seem to help with his current symptoms. He also notes that bending over worsens his symptoms. The patient denies any numbness or tingling in his lower extremities.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports left back pain.
Neurological: Denies any numbness or tingling in the lower extremities.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Musculoskeletal: Examination of the spine reveals no evidence of spinal deformity, tenderness, or muscle spasm. There is no evidence of paraspinal tenderness. There is no evidence of radicular symptoms in the lower extremities.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray images of the lumbar spine reveal no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae. Previous surgical site is visible and appears to have healed properly.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Sean Phillips is a 35-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of left back pain.

Medical Reasoning:
- X-rays were reviewed today and reveal no evidence of fracture or other abnormalities in the spine or vertebrae.
- The patient had a lumbar microdiscectomy performed in November 2020, which likely contributed to his current symptoms.
- The patient has been taking high-dose gabapentin for severe nerve pain through his back and lower extremities prior to the microdiscectomy.
- The patient reports that stretching helps with his symptoms, but stretching does not seem to help with current symptoms.
- Bending over worsens his symptoms.
- There is no evidence of radicular symptoms in the lower extremities.
- I believe this is likely a muscle pull from misalignment in the spine.
- I have prescribed physical therapy for him as he has had great results there before today. We will start with meloxicam instead of ibuprofen as it may help more with pain management today. We will also refer him to pain management for further evaluation and discussion regarding non-opioid options for managing his pain today.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Emily White is a 77-year-old female who presents today for the evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision. The patient reports that she has been experiencing difficulty reading and straight lines, as well as trouble adjusting to dim lights at restaurants. She denies any history of macular degeneration.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Visual: Decreased vision when reading and straight lines.
• Neurological: Trouble adjusting to dim lights at restaurants.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Eyes: Anterior segment examination reveals posterior chamber intraocular lenses in both eyes. The cornea is clear without media opacities. The cup-to-disc ratio is 2 in the right eye and 3 in the left eye. Fundus examination of the right eye shows the retina to be attached without any tears or holes or pigment epithelium changes in the fovea. Posterior segment exam shows drusen in the macula, thickening of the retina, presence of subretinal fluid, exudates accumulation, positive for hemorrhage. Left eye: Cornea is clear without media opacities. No pigment epithelium changes in the fovea. No hemorrhage or subretinal fluid. Retina is attached.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

Optical coherence tomography shows drusen deposit. Retinal pigment epithelium with subretinal fluid accumulation. The choroidal neovascular membrane can be visualized.
Fluorescein angiography reveals focal areas of leakage in the right eye consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

The patient presents today for evaluation of sudden visual distortions and blurring of vision which are consistent with advanced neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

Patient Agreements: The patient understands her diagnosis and treatment options and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.
Medical Treatment Plan: I have reviewed her diagnostic tests and eye exam which are indicative of neovascular age-related macular degeneration which is advanced to a stage that usually leads to more severe vision loss when abnormal blood vessels start to grow beneath the retina and they will leak fluid and blood creating a large blind spot in the center of visual field which is usually caused by smoking, hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol, obesity, family history, radiation exposure, trauma or inflammation.
I have recommended that we proceed with Lucentis injections once a month after numbing with lidocaine after each injection over a period of time this may slow down rate of vision decline or stop further vision loss but however this disease may also progress despite treatment.
Patient Agreements: The patient understands her diagnosis and treatment options and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right ankle pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Jacqueline Price is a 28-year-old female who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right ankle pain. The onset of her symptoms began 3 days ago when she was doing something she did not want to be doing and fell off her bike. She reports that her ankle twisted outward at the time of the fall. She denies any numbness or tingling in her toes. She has been taking Tylenol for pain, but it has not helped. She heard a pop in her ankle at the time of the injury.

PAST HISTORY

Patient reports that she has been mountain biking for 3 years.

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

Patient reports that she is taking Tylenol.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right ankle pain.
Neurological: Reports numbness in her heart.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

VITALS: Temperature: 98.6; Blood Pressure: 118/77; Heart Rate: 77 bpm.
MSK: Examination of the right ankle reveals edema and erythema on the lateral malleolus on the right hand side, associated ecchymosis, and a few excoriations. There is pain to palpation of the right lateral malleolus. There is decreased flexion and extension of the right ankle as well as internal and external rotation. There is no apparent injury to the knee or foot.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
X-ray of the right foot was obtained today and reviewed by me today. The radiographic findings reveal no acute fracture or bony abnormality.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
For your current symptoms, I do believe you have an acute right ankle sprain. We will go ahead and put you in an air cast, prescribe meloxicam fifteen milligrams once a day, ice your area for about twenty minutes five times a day, and weight bear as tolerated. I am anticipating you to start feeling better in the next couple of weeks if you are not to return here and see me again and we will consider physical therapy or pursuing further imaging.

note.subjective:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Myocardial infarction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Betty Garcia is a 72-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of chest pain. The patient reports that he had a myocardial infarction and stent placement in the right coronary artery. He was hospitalized for 48 hours. The patient reports that he has been doing well since returning home, but he continues to experience some shortness of breath when walking up stairs. He denies any chest pain since the stent placement.

The patient reports that his wrist is healing well and there is no infection present.

The patient denies any shortness of breath with exertion.

The patient reports that he takes Brilinta twice a day every 12 hours, aspirin 81 mg at night, Crestor 40 mg once a day, and Toprol 50 mg once a day.

The patient denies any issues with cost with Brilinta.

The patient states that he enjoys swimming but has not been able to do so due to his recent heart attack.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Cardiovascular: Reports chest pain.
Respiratory: Denies shortness of breath with exertion.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neck: No jugular venous distention.
Cardiovascular: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base.
Respiratory: Lungs are clear bilaterally to auscultation.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Inferior myocardial infarction.
- Medical Reasoning: The echocardiogram revealed mild mitral regurgitation which is just a little floppy valve which is fine. Otherwise, everything else for the most part looks good.
- Medical Treatment: Continue aspirin lifelong until further advised. Continue on Brilinta for at least one year and aspirin lifelong until further advised. Continue Crestor 40 mg once a day. Order an echocardiogram in six months for repeat evaluation of mitral regurgitation. Continue Toprol 50 mg once a day as needed for angina symptoms.
- Patient Education and Counseling: Encourage continued light activity and resume swimming with caution after two weeks from cath site healing. Recommend enrollment into cardiac rehab to provide additional confidence and education regarding exercise and diet management.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

note.objective_results:

note.assessment_and_plan:

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Today I have had a lengthy discussion with Mr. Wood regarding his chief complaint and history of present illness. His examination today revealed grade 2/6 systolic murmur with no additional murmurs heard. We discussed his symptoms and reviewed his medical history and current medications in detail today as well.

Mr. Wood presents today with right elbow pain which extends up to his neck and into his left arm. His blood pressure was elevated today at 150/90 mmHg compared to 125/72 mmHg last visit which was likely white coat hypertension as he reports that he has been doing well with diet and exercise recently.

His last A1c was 7.2% which was consistent with type 2 diabetes mellitus and he is currently taking metformin 500 mg daily which has been effective for him thus far but we will obtain a glucose test today to assess glycemic control.

His hypertension is currently being managed with Norvasc 2.5 mg daily which has been effective for him thus far but we will obtain an EKG today to evaluate for possible cardiac etiology for his symptoms.

We discussed all findings in detail today and reviewed all recommendations in detail with him including recommended testing, medications, referrals, etc., prior to obtaining informed consent.

For your first problem of left shoulder pain, your symptoms are most likely due to rotator cuff tendinopathy. This means that the tendons of the muscles of your left shoulder have been injured and the injury happened to the tendons that make up or attach to the shoulder muscles.

Right knee pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Matthew Allen is a 40-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his right knee pain began yesterday after playing basketball. He states that he felt like his knee popped and that he could not bear weight on the leg. He denies any history of prior right knee pain. He reports that he has not played basketball in 2 years and watched the game last night.

The patient reports that his blood pressure was 140/80 this morning. He states that he is taking Norvasc 5 mg daily and Metformin 500 mg daily. He denies taking Tylenol regularly due to gastrointestinal upset.

The patient reports that his A1C was 7.2 last month. He states that he has been eating anything he wants since the pandemic began.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
Cardiovascular: Reports hypertension.
Endocrine: Reports diabetes.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Normal sensation to light touch, vibration, and proprioception in all extremities.
Cardiovascular: Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left lower sternal border, no murmurs heard elsewhere.
Musculoskeletal: Examination of the right knee reveals tenderness to palpation over the medial aspect of the right knee with edema, ecchymosis, and erythema present.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS

X-ray of the right knee was reviewed today and is normal without evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Right knee pain.
- Medical Reasoning: Matthew Allen sustained an MCL strain when playing basketball yesterday. The x-ray was normal without evidence of fractures or bony abnormalities which is good news for him at this time. We will obtain an MRI for further evaluation today as well.
- Patient Education and Counseling: I advised him to continue taking Tylenol for pain management until we obtain his MRI results today. We discussed the importance of taking his blood sugars daily to keep track of them as well as starting a log book to do so. We also discussed the importance of starting Metformin daily as well as increasing his dose from 500 mg due to elevated blood pressure today.
- Medical Treatment Plan: I have prescribed Meloxicam fifteen milligrams for pain and swelling management today as well as a knee immobilizer for him to wear until we obtain his MRI results today.

Elevated Blood Pressure.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient's blood pressure has been elevated and fluctuating recently. His last visit we increased his lisinopril to twice per day but he still experiences episodes of elevated blood pressure.

Hyperlipidemia.

- Medical Treatment: We discussed continued conservative management including walking as tolerated and taking Tylenol for pain if needed. I advised him that if he experiences increased activity level or feels dehydrated then he should increase fluid intake accordingly.

She denies any nasal congestion or runny nose, but does report seasonal allergies. She reports that her headaches are usually rated at 7 out of 10 when they first start, but after taking Tylenol they go down to about a 4 or 5.

The patient denies any history of migraines. She notes that she typically only takes Tylenol for her headaches once every year or two years.

• Headache: Yes.
• Blood Pressure: Elevated.
• Diabetes: Normal blood sugar.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

Neurological: Tenderness over the forehead and cheekbones.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Donna Allen is a 37-year-old female who presents today with complaints of headache. She has a history of hypertension and diabetes.

Medical Reasoning:
- The patient’s headache may be related to her elevated blood pressure as well as her diabetes.
- Her headaches are likely due to tension-type headache given the lack of associated symptoms such as nasal congestion or runny nose.
- Her elevated blood pressure may be due to non-adherence with medication.
- Her elevated blood sugar may be due to increased stress from the headaches.
- The patient’s headaches are likely not migraines based on her history.
- The patient’s tenderness over the forehead and cheekbones suggests sinus tenderness which may be related to sinusitis secondary to allergies.
- The patient’s tenderness in the neck suggests lymphadenopathy secondary to sinusitis secondary to allergies.
- Increased exercise may help with her headaches given that she is already walking regularly.

Patient Agreements:
The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

She has been taking her medication as prescribed, but she has been forgetting to take it regularly.

The patient reports that she has had high blood pressure for a long time and that her provider prescribed her chlorthalidone, but she does not take it because it gives her stomachaches. She also reports that she has been taking metformin for diabetes.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Theresa Rodriguez is a 41-year-old female who presents today for evaluation of uncontrolled hypertension. Her blood pressure was elevated today at 172/98 mmHg. Her heart rate was within normal limits, and her oxygenation was within normal limits. We discussed the importance of diet modification as well as medication adherence today. I recommended that we start with going ahead and continuing her current medication regimen today, but I would like to encourage that she takes it every day and set a reminder on her phone if necessary. We will monitor her blood pressure at home three times per week to see if there is any improvement with the current regimen. I recommended that we schedule a follow-up appointment in one month to reassess her blood pressure at this point in time.
Regarding her diabetes, we discussed dietary modifications as well as increasing the dose of metformin to fifteen hundred milligrams daily. We will continue monitoring her blood sugars to ensure that the change in medication is effective.

Surgical: Denies history of surgery.

Neurological:

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Steven Reed is a 60-year-old male who presents today for evaluation of chronic lumbar back pain based on his symptoms, exam, and reviewing his MRI results which are consistent with a herniated disk at L4-L5 with radiculopathy. We discussed this today and I recommended that we proceed with a spinal injection with a strong anti-inflammatory medication called a corticosteroid. We discussed that this is something that you had before but it did not seem to be as effective as we would have liked so I think this steroid shot is the best chance that we have. We also discussed that if after this injection you still are experiencing pain then we can explore other options such as pain medication however I would recommend surgery if needed after trying everything else first. We will schedule an appointment for you to come in for your procedure today.

Right knee contusion.

Joe Reed is a 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of right knee pain. The onset of his symptoms began over the weekend on Saturday. note.objective_results:
RESULTS

note.assessment_and_plan:

Joe Reed is a 42-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for evaluation of right knee contusion.

Imaging findings reveal no fractures or bony abnormalities.
Impression: Right knee contusion.
Plan: Rest, ice, elevation, and NSAIDs such as ibuprofen every 6-8 hours as needed for pain management. If symptoms do not improve with conservative measures, we will follow up again in clinic for further evaluation including physical therapy if needed.
Patient Agreements.

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Follow-up of nonsmall cell lung cancer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

Angela King is a 58-year-old female who presents today for follow-up of nonsmall cell lung cancer. She reports that she has been experiencing shortness of breath over the weekend. She had previously been very active, taking mile-long walks with her doberman. Her husband has been her support system and her daughter has also been helpful. She is currently taking cisplatin, etoposide, and Zofran.

The patient reports that she has been coughing but denies phlegm. She denies fever. She does report pain when swallowing, which she describes as a sharp pain in her chest when swallowing. She denies any body aches or sore throat.

The patient reports that she is doing okay on her chemotherapy regimen, but notes that she was nauseated and tired after her last dose of chemotherapy today. She took Zofran and felt better afterwards.

On a mental/emotional standpoint, the patient reports that she is devastated with the diagnosis and is trying to figure everything out. However, she notes that her husband has been very supportive and helpful.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS

• Constitutional: Denies fever.
• Respiratory: Reports shortness of breath, dry cough, dysphagia.
note.objective_exam:
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
• Neck: No cervical lymphadenopathy or subclavicular adenopathy.
• Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs.
• Respiratory: Crackles in bilateral lungs.
note.objective_results:
RESULTS
• Chest x-ray obtained today shows mild radiation pneumonitis.
note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
• Nonsmall cell lung cancer.
- Medical Reasoning: The patient presents today for follow-up of nonsmall cell lung cancer. Her most recent pathology report shows evidence of a 4.4 cm left upper lobe nodule; chest x-ray obtained today shows mild radiation pneumonitis.
- Medical Treatment: We will continue the current neo-adjuvant chemotherapy regimen with cisplatin and etoposide as tolerated. We will also continue radiation therapy at 45 Gy in fractions to target the left upper lobe nodule as tolerated until tumor shrinkage is noted on imaging studies. We will discontinue radiation therapy once tumor shrinkage is noted on imaging studies due to the risk of radiation pneumonitis from prolonged steroid use.
- Patient Education/ Counseling: I have counseled the patient on the importance of maintaining adequate hydration while undergoing chemotherapy due to risk for dehydration from mucositis secondary to chemotherapy treatment.
- Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with recommended medical treatment plan.

• Constitutional: Denies fevers, chills.

• Patient Agreements: The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan.

note.assessment_and_plan:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

Frank Lee is a 54-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for shortness of breath. The onset of his symptoms began about 1 week ago. His history is significant for coronary disease, acute myocardial infarction in 2018, placement of a coronary artery stent in the right coronary artery in 2018, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease. His current medications include Lasix 40 mg once a day.

His examination reveals grade 3 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base and grade 1-2 pitting edema bilaterally on examination. His blood pressure is elevated at this time, measuring at 135/80 mmHg. We discussed dietary modifications today including reducing salt intake and avoiding NSAIDs due to his chronic kidney disease.
